item.title: Morning Bid: All eyes on AI
item.description: A look at the day ahead in European and global markets from Ankur Banerjee
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A look at the day ahead in European and global markets from Ankur Banerjee Markets are basking in the afterglow of the blockbuster [USN:L6N46C148 TEXT:"US IPO filing"] of Claude-developer [USN:L3N46C10M TEXT:"Anthropic"] that has lifted the mood weighing on investor sentiment regarding the [USN:L6N46C0RS TEXT:"debt-fuelled AI trade"]. Asian stocks took cues from Wall Street as investors cheered [USN:L3N46C1YC TEXT:"Anthropic"] unveiling its US initial public offering paperwork on Monday, a much-awaited filing that comes as scrutiny over huge AI spending has surged and worry over fundraising swirled. The IPO filing didn't reveal anything we didn't know. Eye-popping revenue growth. Check. Staggering loss. Check. Risk factor [USN:L6N45L01K TEXT:"detailing possible end of the world"] as we know it. Erm, also check. Not to be outdone, Facebook parent Meta Platforms (META.O) [USN:L3N46C0RT TEXT:"plans"] to raise up to a record $95 billion to fund AI infrastructure expansion. And SpaceX (SPCX.O) said an affiliate of Apollo Global Management (APO.N) will buy AI chips and server hardware and lease them to the rockets-to-AI firm, in a deal with total principal payments of about $40 billion. While the fundraising has allayed some worry, it also adds to concern about the incredible capital needed for AI infrastructure and how quickly it may become profitable. Just last week, the cost of insuring Meta's debt against default [USN:L4N4681N3 TEXT:"touched"] an all-time high. For now, traders have their risk-on hat on, taking South Korea's KOSPI (.KS11) , the epicentre of the AI boom in Asia, 3.6% higher in its biggest one-day jump since early September. The index, dominated by AI chip bellwethers Samsung Electronics (005930.KS) and SK Hynix (000660.KS) , is still set for a 17% decline in October, underscoring the AI jitters. The strong start for risk assets on Tuesday sets the stage for a pivotal week where earnings from AI hyperscalers and policy decisions from major central banks will set the tone for trading for the rest of the year. Market watchers expect policymakers in New Zealand and Canada to hike interest rates by 25 basis points, and those in the US, euro zone and Japan to keep them on hold but signal possible increases in December. Investors have been focusing on AI fear recently, shrugging off inflation concern and running for the safety of government bonds, especially Treasuries. That has pushed the yield on the 10-year note below 5% but perhaps cautionary words from central bankers might stoke inflation worry too. Key developments that could influence markets on Tuesday: October consumer confidence for France Novartis earnings

item.title: Moody's sees positive shift in Japan's growth, resilience remains key test
item.description: Moody's sees encouraging signs in Japan's return to sustained growth and stable inflation, but a key test will be whether that resilience can withstand future shocks, the rating agency's Japan sovereign analyst told Reuters on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Makiko Yamazaki
item.content:encoded: Moody's sees encouraging signs in Japan's return to sustained growth and stable inflation, but a key test will be whether that resilience can withstand future shocks, the rating agency's Japan sovereign analyst told Reuters on Tuesday. Moody's rates Japan at A1, its fifth-highest investment-grade rating, with a stable outlook, unchanged since its 2014 downgrade of Japan from Aa3. "We're starting to see what looks more like sustained growth and inflation expectations that are reasonably well anchored around 2%," said Martin Petch, a vice president at the sovereign risk group of Moody's Ratings. "That's been something that's changed," Petch said in an interview, referring to a shift from decades of weak growth and chronically low inflation. Petch declined to speculate on future rating actions, but said Moody's was watching to see if recent changes in Japan's economic and inflation environment prove sustainable, along with reforms that boost productivity and tackle demographic woes. A key test, he added, is whether Japan can maintain growth and inflation stability through future economic shocks. "You can generally tell when growth has become sustained when the economy has dealt with a shock," Petch said, pointing out that Japan had coped well with recent energy-price shocks while the central bank keeps up efforts to normalise policy. LITTLE IMMEDIATE THREAT SEEN TO CREDIT PROFILE Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's food sales tax cut and ambitious spending plans rattled bond markets this year, but Petch suggested the measures have posed little immediate threat to Japan's credit profile. Their fiscal impact would depend on whether the government delivered on its pledge to offset the resulting revenue loss, he added. Although ministries have sought a record 143 trillion yen ($908 billion) in initial spending requests, Petch said the rise was relatively modest compared with combined initial and supplementary budgets. This reinforced Moody's view that there has been no meaningful departure from Japan's recent consolidation trend, he added. But uncertainties hover over the government's 370-trillion-yen public-private investment initiative, Petch said. These include the extent to which the private sector joins the initiative, and whether it can bring the productivity gains needed to offset Japan's demographic headwinds, he added. ($1=157.4700 yen)

item.title: IEA flags concentration of clean energy supply chains as emerging challenge
item.description: The concentration of a small number of countries in clean energy supply chains is an emerging challenge for Southeast Asian countries, International Energy Agency Executive Director Fatih Birol said on Tuesday, amid fast-rising power demand in the region.
item.dc:creator: Siyi Liu, Florence Tan
item.content:encoded: The concentration of a small number of countries in clean energy supply chains is an emerging challenge for Southeast Asian countries, International Energy Agency Executive Director Fatih Birol said on Tuesday, amid fast-rising power demand in the region. "The age of electricity is coming. We will still use oil, still use natural gas including LNG, but electricity demand is growing very strongly," Birol told delegates at the Singapore International Energy Week conference. Birol did not identify the countries dominating clean energy supplies, but China is by far the largest global supplier of renewable energy equipment, from solar panels to wind turbines, electric vehicles and batteries. Electricity demand in ASEAN countries is rising at twice the pace of overall energy consumption, driven by industrial electrification, air-conditioning needs, electric vehicles and data centres, he said. Southeast Asian nations have emerged as[USN:L1N3A320I TEXT:" key drivers of China's clean-energy export boom"], splashing out over $20 billion on Chinese-made clean-tech products so far in 2026, according to energy think tank Ember. Birol also warned that geopolitical tensions have become an increasingly dominant force in global energy markets. "In my professional life, I have never, never ever seen the dark and long shadow of geopolitics dominating the energy sector in such a way," he said. "I can only imagine that the role of geopolitics will be much more pronounced, and this means energy security is going to become even more important than it is today." Birol said the Middle East war has triggered fundamental changes in global energy consumption patterns, spurring growth in solar, coal and nuclear power as well as electric vehicle adoption. "I see in the last eight months very strong growth of electric car sales," he said, adding that global electric vehicle sales outside China had risen 60% above previous trends over the period because of the conflict. Consumption of alternative energy sources has increased as diesel prices have jumped about 200% and LNG prices have risen 250% from pre-war levels, according to Birol. He [USN:L2N46C04R TEXT:"said on Monday"] at the same conference that he does not expect energy markets in 2027 to return to where they were before the US-Israeli war on Iran began.

item.title: Top doubles players call on ATP to rethink proposed changes
item.description: Leading men's doubles players have called on the ATP Tour to reconsider plans that would reduce the size of the doubles competitions at events and move prize money to the singles format.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Leading men's doubles players have called on the ATP Tour to reconsider plans that would reduce the size of the doubles competitions at events and move prize money to the singles format. In a letter addressed to the ATP board and management and signed by 137 active players, 33 former players and 20 federations, the group said it understood the need for reforms but was deeply concerned about the plans being discussed. The ATP said this month it was reviewing potential changes to the size of the doubles draws at tournaments as part of its [USN:L4N4610DJ TEXT:"plans for 2028"] and beyond, with the freed-up funds going towards singles qualifying and early-round prize money. "The current plans would shift about $20 million in prize money from doubles to singles, while cutting a significant number of professional opportunities for doubles specialists," the group wrote. "That shift would make it much harder for talented players to build and sustain a doubles career. A healthy professional sport cannot rely solely on a small group of top stars; it needs pathways for players to develop, compete and earn a living." Reuters has contacted the ATP for comment. The governing body of men's tennis said earlier this month doubles will continue to be a core part of the tour and its reviews were focused on identifying a model for its sustainable long-term future. It added that discussions would continue with the Player Advisory Council. The ATP is set to hold its year-end meetings in Turin next month. The plans being discussed include cutting the number of doubles teams at elite ATP Masters 1000 events to 16 from 32, with events below that level featuring smaller fields. Apart from the Grand Slams and Olympic Games, doubles receives much less attention than singles and few top singles players commit to playing the format, though it is hugely popular at club level. Dutch player Sem Verbeek said the ATP should look after the interests of all its members. "Tennis is more than a business," the doubles world number 60 said on X. "It's a legacy built on joy, health and sportsmanship. A sport built on those values should open doors, not close them." The ATP outlined plans this month to boost its bonus pool to $50 million from $21.5 million, and reshape its rankings and calendar as part of a package aimed at lifting player compensation to $350 million from 2028.

item.title: Citi, Visa still matter to China, and vice versa
item.description: Beijing is opening up to the US duo: an onshore securities business for the bank and bank card clearing for the payments giant. It’s overdue but both can profit from the $20 trln economy and its outbound ambitions through global networks Chinese rivals cannot easily replicate.
item.dc:creator: Ka Sing Chan
item.content:encoded: Beijing is granting key approvals to US financial giants as it looks for areas of pragmatic cooperation with Washington. For Citigroup (C.N) , the bank led by Jane Fraser, it is a licence to establish a wholly-owned securities company. For payments giant Visa (V.N) , led by Ryan McInerney, it is permission to begin preparations for a domestic bank card clearing institution. China's latest opening is long overdue but remains valuable. There's a realpolitik to the timing. The all-clear from officials comes just weeks after Xi Jinping's state visit to the US. McInerney and Fraser both joined the US delegation to China in May when President Trump said he raised Visa's market access plight with his counterpart. Since June, the Visa boss has chaired the US-China Business Council. A decade ago, Visa would have benefited tremendously from a domestic clearing licence. Back then, mobile phones accounted for less than 10% of China’s retail payments. Today, payment apps operated by the likes of Alibaba (9988.HK) and Tencent (0700.HK) represent nearly 90% of spending in China. Visa's opportunity now lies less in displacing incumbents than in helping money move across borders. Its global network supports overseas travel, international e-commerce and digital-payment services such as tokenization, which helps secure transactions across merchants and markets. That reach is difficult for Chinese companies to replicate. Even the state-run UnionPay, which handles about 95% of the country's card spending, has forged partnerships with Visa in international remittances and tourism payments. Though Citi fell behind its US rivals in China after exiting a joint venture with Orient Securities (600958.SS) in 2019 and applying to operate on its own, the $200 billion lender is re-entering the onshore investment banking business at a time foreign firms' fortunes have been improving. The wholly-owned units of Goldman Sachs (GS.N) , JPMorgan (JPM.N) and UBS (UBSG.S) all posted sharp profit rebounds in 2025 as market activity recovered and overseas investors returned; Goldman logged a $219 million net profit on current exchange rates. By the end of June, foreign investors held 4.66 trillion yuan of Chinese equities, up 26% from December and 60% from the end of 2024, PBOC data shows. The new licence fills a gap in a franchise that is Citi's second largest internationally after the UK. It already banks many of the world's largest multinationals and asset managers. Those relationships should, on paper, give it an advantage over pure-play investment banks once the new venture is up and running. Ultimately, the US duo can also support China Inc's global investment push. China still needs firms that connect it to global capital and commerce. The licences may have arrived late. The rationale for them did not. Citigroup Inc. said on October 23 it has received approval from the China Securities Regulatory Commission to establish a wholly-owned securities company in China. Visa Inc. has received approval to begin preparations for a domestic bank card clearing institution in the country, the People’s Bank of China said on October 13. CONTEXT-NEWS

item.title: Ty Jerome’s late free throws carry Grizzlies past Jazz
item.description: Ty Jerome scored eight of his 15 points in the final six minutes -- including two clutch free throws with 11.6 seconds remaining -- to lead the Memphis Grizzlies to a 110-105 victory Monday over the Utah Jazz. The Grizzlies won their fourth straight game to open the season for only the second time in franchise history.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Ty Jerome scored eight of his 15 points in the final six minutes -- including two clutch free throws with 11.6 seconds remaining -- to lead the Memphis Grizzlies to a 110-105 victory Monday over the Utah Jazz. The Grizzlies won their fourth straight game to open the season for only the second time in franchise history. Cedric Coward had 16 points and 11 rebounds, Jaylen Wells added 14 points and Cam Boozer and Jerami Grant each scored 13 for Memphis. Keyonte George had 26 points for the Jazz and Ace Bailey contributed 17 points and 10 boards. Mo Bamba added 14 points and seven rebounds off the bench. Utah lost two starters in the first half to injury. Jaren Jackson Jr., the former Grizzlies' star, injured his right knee in the second quarter and did not return. Lauri Markkanen injured his right wrist early in the first quarter and did not return. The Grizzlies never trailed after taking the lead midway through the first quarter. Utah rallied in the fourth to trim the deficit to one point on two occasions, the last coming with 1:01 remaining following a shot by Bamba. Two free throws by Wells with 41 seconds left put Memphis ahead 108-105 before Jerome sank two more with 11.6 to go. Memphis led by six at halftime before Utah trimmed the Grizzlies lead to one (58-57) early in the third quarter on a three-point play by George. The Grizzlies gradually extended their lead to 10 points late in the third quarter (76-66) following a driving dunk from reserve center Quinten Post. Memphis led by 13 entering the fourth quarter after Post converted on an in-bounds lob. The Grizzlies built a 15-point lead at 45-30 in the second quarter behind the long-range shooting of Jerami Grant. He had two 3-pointers during the first minutes of the quarter. Utah rallied to cut its deficit to six points (58-52) at halftime. George had 17 points at the break. --Field Level Media

item.title: Germany's Merz says EU has strategic interest in open market access
item.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said on Tuesday that the European Union, with its 450 million consumers, has strategic interests in collaborating on open access to markets, including with members of the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership pact.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said on Tuesday that the European Union, with its 450 million consumers, has strategic interests in collaborating on open access to markets, including with members of the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership pact. Because of a changing world, the EU is seeking closer partnerships, including with the Southeast Asian bloc ASEAN, Merz said at a press conference during a visit to Singapore.

item.title: HSBC's third-quarter profit jumps 32%, launches buyback of up to $1 billion
item.description: HSBC reported a 32% surge in third-quarter profit on Tuesday as rate hikes supported net interest income and due to the absence of legal provisions booked in the same period a year earlier.
item.dc:creator: Selena Li, Lawrence White
item.content:encoded: HSBC (HSBA.L) reported a 32% surge in third-quarter profit on Tuesday as rate hikes supported net interest income and due to the absence of legal provisions booked in the same period a year earlier. Europe's largest bank also unveiled a share buyback of up to $1 billion, the same amount as the previous quarter. Pretax profit came in at $9.6 billion for the July-September quarter, in line with estimates compiled by HSBC. The bank also said expected credit losses tumbled 17% to $800 million rom the same period a year ago, thanks to a reduction in charges linked to Hong Kong's real estate sector as well as its UK and Mexican wealth businesses. HSBC announced an interim dividend of $0.1 per share, the same as the previous quarter.

item.title: Matvei Gridin scores twice as Flames defeat Maple Leafs
item.description: The Calgary Flames held on to top the visiting Toronto Maple Leafs 5-2 on Monday night. Matvei Gridin scored two goals and an assist as Calgary won its fourth straight.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Calgary Flames held on to top the visiting Toronto Maple Leafs 5-2 on Monday night. Matvei Gridin scored two goals and an assist as Calgary won its fourth straight. William Nylander brought the Maple Leafs within a goal 6:06 into the third, Jack Roslovic forking the puck onto the Calgary's native stick with a one-handed pass through a maze of bodies. The home team responded with two empty-netters near the end of the game to close it out. Captain Mikael Backlund scored to move into a fifth-place tie with Johnny Gaudreau for all-time points as a Calgary Flame. Joel Farabee and Martin Pospisil had a goal and an assist each while Matt Coronato and Simon Nemec added two helpers. Easton Cowan also scored for the Maple Leafs. Calgary's Devin Cooley made 26 saves and received credit for an assist. Toronto's Sergei Bobrovsky had 29 saves on 32 shots. Gridin opened the scoring 10:05 into the game, driving into the offensive zone on the outside and launching the puck over the shoulder of Bobrovsky from a tight angle. Backlund made it 2-0 1:45 later when Cowan coughed up the puck in his own end. Coronato played the puck through the slot and onto the tape of the Calgary captain, who was returning from a two-game injury absence. Just 25 seconds into the middle frame, Zayne Parekh played a long stretch pass up to Gridin, who wristed it past Bobrovsky once again to put the Flames up three on the power play. Troy Stecher sent a slap pass to Cowan speeding towards goal. The 21-year-old sophomore outmuscled Aydar Suniev and tipped the puck into the net moments before colliding with an outstretched Cooley 12:54 into the second period. Farabee put the game away with an empty-netter with 1:25 remaining. Pospisil added another empty-net goal with 39 seconds left. Maple Leafs winger Kirill Marchenko left the game with a lower-body injury after an awkward fall early in the second period. The game marked the Maple Leafs' final regular-season appearance at the Scotiabank Saddledome. --Field Level Media

item.title: CDC deputy director to leave Trump administration, paper says
item.description: Jennifer Shuford, the deputy director of the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, will leave the Trump administration after next week's midterm elections, the Washington Post said on Monday, citing sources.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Jennifer Shuford, the deputy director of the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, will leave the Trump administration after next week's [TOPIC:"reuters:/world/us/elections/" TEXT:"midterm elections"], the Washington Post said on Monday, citing sources. The departure follows changes in the government's vaccine policy, with President Donald Trump [USN:L1N45A0WN TEXT:"unveiling"] plans to demand that vaccine makers split certain childhood shots into five separate doses. The CDC and the White House did not respond to requests for comment outside business hours. A former Texas health commissioner, Shuford, who is also the CDC's chief medical officer, was [USN:L1N40Z161 TEXT:"hired"] in April among a team including former deputy surgeon general Erica Schwartz, healthcare executive Sean Slovenski, and FDA official Sara Brenner. The reason for Shuford's departure was not immediately clear, the paper said, citing one person as attributing it to a family health issue, while another said she had disagreed with the administration’s approach to vaccine policy. The step flagged by Trump would advance a long-standing goal of Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., an anti-vaccine activist who has promoted a link between vaccines and autism that scientists have repeatedly debunked.

item.title: Alibaba wins injunction against Pentagon contract restrictions tied to China blacklist
item.description: A US federal judge on Monday granted Alibaba Group Holding's request for a preliminary injunction, ordering the US government not to deny Pentagon contracts to companies because they, their parent companies or subsidiaries do business with firms that engage in lobbying activities for the e-commerce giant.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Baptista, Preetika Parashuraman
item.content:encoded: A US federal judge on Monday granted Alibaba Group Holding's (9988.HK) request for a preliminary injunction, ordering the US government not to deny Pentagon contracts to companies because they, their parent companies or subsidiaries do business with firms that engage in lobbying activities for the e-commerce giant. Alibaba [USN:L1N42V0RB TEXT:"sued"] the US government in June after the Pentagon added it to a [USN:FWN42G12Z TEXT:"list of companies"] allegedly aiding China's military, alongside internet search provider Baidu, EV maker BYD, and other major Chinese manufacturing and technology firms. Monday's ruling means Alibaba will be able to retain US lobbyists who also represent Pentagon contractors, removing a potential obstacle to the company's efforts to challenge its designation as a Chinese military company. The designation does not impose formal sanctions, but restricts Pentagon contracts with listed companies and, from 2027, purchases of their products or services through third parties. Alibaba has denied any military ties, saying its products and services are built for retail, logistics, and enterprise technology rather than defence or intelligence. "The determinations have no basis in fact or law," Alibaba said in its lawsuit in June, seeking its removal from the list. Monday's injunction does not remove Alibaba from the Pentagon list, which the company is continuing to challenge in court. Alibaba did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the injunction.

item.title: Alperen Sengun nets 29 as Rockets remain perfect with win over Hawks
item.description: Alperen Sengun scored a game-high 29 points, Jabari Smith Jr. added a double-double, and the Houston Rockets remained unbeaten by beating the visiting Atlanta Hawks 120-110 on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Alperen Sengun scored a game-high 29 points, Jabari Smith Jr. added a double-double, and the Houston Rockets remained unbeaten by beating the visiting Atlanta Hawks 120-110 on Monday. Sengun added nine rebounds and nine assists to pace a balanced attack. He was instrumental during a 14-2 run that helped the Rockets establish a working margin in the third quarter, and his transition dunk in the fourth fueled a 20-2 rally that lifted the Rockets to a 115-95 lead. Smith paired 16 points with 12 rebounds, while Kevin Durant added 22 points and nine boards. Tari Eason and Reed Sheppard scored 13 points apiece off the Houston bench. Jalen Johnson paced the Hawks with 21 points and nine rebounds while CJ McCollum added 20 points and four 3-pointers. The Hawks dropped back-to-back games against the Rockets. Luguentz Dort (11 points) and Nickell Alexander-Walker (12 points) teamed to pull the Hawks to within 95-93 in the fourth quarter before Sheppard drilled a 3-pointer and Smith followed with a three-point play after dunking through a foul. Smith assisted on the aforementioned Sengun dunk before Eason and Sheppard added 3-pointers that extended the lead to 20. Eason grabbed eight rebounds. Amen Thompson paired 15 points with five rebounds as the Rockets shot 53.1% from the floor and scored 26 points in transition. There were five lead changes and two ties in the third before the Rockets took control with their run. The Hawks erased an early five-point deficit with 3-pointers from Onyeka Okongwu and Johnson, and seized a three-point lead that they carried through the end of the first quarter. Sheppard sparked the Rockets in the second period with a nifty reverse layup through a foul and a steal that Durant converted into a free throw and a 44-41 lead. But McCollum helped the Hawks respond with a floater and a 3-pointer to tie the game at 46-46, and Atlanta reclaimed a 66-63 lead at the intermission after the Rockets missed 12 of 16 3-pointers in the opening half. --Field Level Media

item.title: Taiwan rebuffs China's commemorations for post-World War Two 'restoration' of island
item.description: Taiwan's defence minister on Tuesday said China was waging "cognitive warfare" after Beijing marked the anniversary of Japan's handover of the island to Chinese rule with satellite images of Taipei and a military propaganda poster.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Taiwan's defence minister on Tuesday said China was waging "cognitive warfare" after Beijing marked the anniversary of Japan's handover of the island to Chinese rule with satellite images of Taipei and a military propaganda poster. Japan took over Taiwan from China's Qing Dynasty in 1895 and ruled it until 1945, when it transferred the island to the Republic of China government. Both Beijing and Taipei commemorate the event, now in its 81st year. On Sunday's anniversary of the handover, China released high-resolution satellite pictures of Taipei, including the train station and the National Palace Museum. The museum holds a vast collection of treasures brought to Taiwan in 1949, when the Republic of China government fled there after losing a civil war to the communists. The Chinese military's Eastern Theatre Command also published a poster with a map of Taiwan superimposed on images of fighter jets and warships, with the title "Remember the history of the restoration". Speaking to reporters at parliament in Taipei, Taiwan Defence Minister Wellington Koo said China was using the anniversary to carry out "cognitive warfare". "We must stress that the People's Republic of China was established in 1949. The War of Resistance has absolutely nothing to do with the People's Republic of China — this is a clear, objective fact," he added, referring to World War Two and the Japanese invasion of China which began in 1931. Taiwan's military marked a different anniversary, the start of an unsuccessful late-October 1949 invasion attempt by the People's Liberation Army of Kinmen, islands which sit next to the Chinese coast and remain under Taiwan control to this day. Koo said that was a date much more worthy of remembering. "This reminds us once again that China's determination to annex the Republic of China and Taiwan by force has never changed. We should be even more vigilant," he added. Beijing has never renounced the use of force to bring Taiwan under its control. The democratically elected government in Taipei rejects Beijing's sovereignty claims. Neither government formally recognises the other, and their shared World War Two history is a frequent [USN:L4N45M05D TEXT:"source"] of [USN:L4N45J003 TEXT:"tension"].

item.title: Dak Prescott (3 TDs), Cowboys hand Eagles' fifth straight loss
item.description: Dak Prescott threw three touchdown passes, Javonte Williams ran for a career-high 155 yards and the Dallas Cowboys pulled away for a 38-21 road win Monday night against the Philadelphia Eagles.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Dak Prescott threw three touchdown passes, Javonte Williams ran for a career-high 155 yards and the Dallas Cowboys pulled away for a 38-21 road win Monday night against the Philadelphia Eagles. The Cowboys (3-4) snapped a two-game skid as Prescott passed for 212 yards with two TDs to CeeDee Lamb and one to George Pickens. They racked up a season-high 204 rushing yards and outgained their NFC East rivals 416-321. The Eagles (2-5) have dropped five straight for the first time since 2016. One week after learning that Jalen Hurts was out for the season with blood clots, Philadelphia put up an early fight and briefly led in the third quarter before allowing 18 unanswered points. Making his fourth NFL start, Tanner McKee threw for 211 yards with a touchdown to Makai Lemon and one interception. Saquon Barkley was used cautiously after missing two games with a hamstring injury, turning nine touches into 71 yards from scrimmage and a rushing score. McKee started the second half with a 17-play, 84-yard drive that took 9:16 off the clock, capping it with a 4-yard TD toss to the rookie Lemon for a 21-20 Eagles lead. It was all Dallas after that. Prescott floated a 16-yard touchdown pass to Lamb and then ran in the two-point conversion to put the Cowboys up 28-21 late in the third quarter -- the game's sixth lead change. Brandon Aubrey's third field goal from 24 yards extended the Cowboys' cushion to 31-21 with 9:10 left in the fourth quarter, and Williams punctuated his career night with a 2-yard TD run with 2:21 remaining. The Cowboys did not turn the ball over and won for the first time in four primetime games this season. After Dallas opened the scoring with Aubrey's 55-yard field goal, Philadelphia tallied its first opening-drive points of the season on Barkley's 8-yard touchdown run. Barkley ignited the drive with a 29-yard run on his first carry since Week 4. The Cowboys answered with Prescott's 9-yard scoring strike to Lamb for a 10-7 lead with 5:32 left in the first quarter. The Eagles made it 14-10 early in the second quarter on a 5-yard TD run by Dameon Pierce. The Cowboys scored the next 10 points for a 20-14 lead at intermission. Prescott fired a 21-yard scoring dart to Pickens and Aubrey added a 27-yard field goal on the final play of the half. --Field Level Media

item.title: Jackson Chourio, Brewers blitz Rays in Game 3, close in on Series sweep
item.description: ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. -- Jackson Chourio highlighted his four-hit performance with an RBI double to cap an eight-run fifth inning, fueling Milwaukee to a 10-1 romp over the Tampa Bay Rays on Monday as the Brewers took a three-games-to-none lead in the World Series.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. -- Jackson Chourio highlighted his four-hit performance with an RBI double to cap an eight-run fifth inning, fueling Milwaukee to a 10-1 romp over the Tampa Bay Rays on Monday as the Brewers took a three-games-to-none lead in the World Series. Chourio is 8-for-14 with four runs in the first three contests of the Fall Classic for Milwaukee, which holds a 3-0 lead in the best-of-seven series. The Brewers, who are 10-1 in the postseason, will look to capture their first World Series title in Game 4 on Tuesday in St. Petersburg. Milwaukee recorded 16 hits to provide more than enough offense for Robert Gasser (1-0), who allowed one hit -- Yandy Diaz's single to lead off the first -- over six scoreless innings. He walked one and struck out three. Gasser has yielded one run on seven hits in 15 innings over three outings in the postseason. The Brewers broke open the game in the fifth after a replay review overturned a call at second base in which a hustling Christian Yelich initially was called out to end the inning. Instead, Milwaukee had the bases loaded, and the Brewers turned a 2-0 game into a 10-0 laugher when each of the next six batters reached base. Cam Booser relieved Freddy Peralta (2-1) and promptly permitted a sharp single by Brice Turang that caromed off the glove of shortstop Taylor Walls and into shallow center field, allowing Chourio and Yelich to score. Garrett Mitchell added an RBI single to left field, Cooper Pratt bounced a two-run double over the third base bag, and Sal Frelick delivered an RBI double to extend the Brewers' lead to 8-0. That chased Booser, but David Hamilton greeted Cole Sulser with an RBI single and Chourio added a run-scoring double to push Milwaukee's advantage to 10-0. Chourio singled off Peralta with one out in the third inning, advanced to second on a walk by Jake Bauers and opened the scoring on Yelich's single to left field. Milwaukee doubled the advantage on the next pitch when William Contreras singled to right field. Victor Mesa Jr. briefly bobbled the ball, allowing Bauers to score from second base. Peralta permitted five runs on seven hits in 4 2/3 innings against the team with which he spent the first eight seasons of his major league career. Diaz had an RBI double in the ninth inning off Brewers veteran Brandon Woodruff, who hadn't pitched since July 4 due to a shoulder injury. --Field Level Media

item.title: Judge extends block on Trump plans to renovate Washington golf course
item.description: A US judge extended on Monday a court order blocking President Donald Trump's plans to renovate a historic Washington golf course where she had deemed a removal of trees "inexcusable".
item.dc:creator: Kanishka Singh
item.content:encoded: A US judge extended on Monday a court order blocking President Donald Trump's plans to renovate a [USN:L6N46503C TEXT:"historic Washington golf course"] where [USN:L1N45Y0L4 TEXT:"she had deemed"] a removal of trees "inexcusable". The renovation, at the center of a lawsuit over environmental and historic preservation concerns, is one of the projects Trump is pursuing to reshape landmarks in the US capital. "The court still does not speak for the trees," US District Judge Ana Reyes said in her order filed in the district court for the District of Columbia, adding, "It speaks only for the rule of law." Her order barred the government from "removing or damaging additional trees" on the course. It also ordered the government to provide 10 business days' of written advance notice before it makes any "irreparable modification" at the park, pending the suit outcome. Two weeks earlier, Reyes faulted the conduct of Justice Department lawyers in the lawsuit seeking to halt the Trump administration's takeover of the historic golf course. It was "inexcusable" that hundreds of trees were removed from the course during the prior weekend, she added. Last week Trump said his administration [USN:L6N46503C TEXT:"would begin renovation"] work immediately, despite the judge's order that work could not proceed without prior notice to the court. In an online post, Trump declared his administration had "an absolute right" to proceed, while blasting the judge as "lunatic," and calling the lawsuit "ridiculous." The DC Preservation League sued in February to halt the takeover, on the grounds that it would violate environmental laws and "irreparably destroy a priceless piece of American history." Reyes said the government had asked her to disregard Trump's statements about the renovation plans. "Rarely, if ever, has the United States Department of Justice urged a federal court not to believe the sitting president," Reyes said. "This started as a case about golf ... But it has become much more," she added. "It now forces the court to reconcile assertions by President Donald J. Trump with the sworn testimony of multiple government employees and the argument of senior DOJ attorneys."

item.title: Palliser’s Samsung buyback bet puts a hat on a hat
item.description: The activist wants the South Korean titan to sop up $100 bln of preferred shares but overcomplicates the play by calling for the issuance of US ADRs to fund it. Demanding ordinary shares' exclusion from repurchases also risks driving a wedge between foreign and local investors.
item.dc:creator: Hudson Lockett
item.content:encoded: In comedy writing, “putting a hat on a hat” can describe needlessly complicating a straightforward joke. Palliser Capital has done much the same in its push for Samsung Electronics (005930.KS) to repurchase second-class shares on the cheap. The underlying logic is sound. The UK-based activist wants Samsung, which will report its earnings on Thursday, to repurchase some 132 trillion won ($100 billion) in non-voting preferred shares. These were originally issued decades ago by the South Korean maker of semiconductors and mobile handsets to raise funds without diluting existing shareholders’ voting power, and account for 12% of shares outstanding. But they trade at a heavy 23% discount to ordinary shares, in part because they offer negligible dividend advantage. Palliser’s call coincides with intense pressure on Samsung to step up returns for ordinary shareholders following record artificial intelligence-powered profits. The company has already announced a record return policy of up to 110 trillion won for the current fiscal year, with 30 trillion won dedicated to third-quarter cash dividends for all shareholders. Using the entire remainder to snap up and cancel cheaper preferred shares, the activist argues, can deliver more bang for each buck while shrinking the number of total shares and boosting dividend payments. Specifically, Palliser wants Samsung to commit to a preferred share discount target – as the chipmaker did in 2015 – and reckons the company can eliminate the gap completely and eventually re-acquire the entire class of stock by 2028. Before that, the activist estimates preferred shareholders could see a share price bump of 84%, compared to 37% for ordinary shareholders. It’s a fair point, but the optics are awful: foreign investors accounted for 73% of preferred shareholders at the end of June, compared to 46% of common shares. That makes full-throated support from the administration of President Lee Jae Myung less certain, even with local fund Life Asset Management making the same demand . Lee wants conglomerates to pony up more returns but his constituents are South Korean voters, not foreign funds. Palliser adds another needless twist by calling on Samsung to issue American Depositary Receipts and use proceeds exclusively for preferred stock buybacks. In July, rival SK Hynix (000660.KS) raised $26.5 billion from its own US debut, with those shares now trading at a more than 40% premium to their Seoul-listed counterparts. Yet with Samsung tipped by Visible Alpha to end the year with cash and cash equivalents of roughly $147 billion, the firm has little need to tap American investors and dilute existing shareholders at home. Palliser can be commended for holding Samsung’s feet to the fire, but risks overplaying its hand in a market that’s [USN:L6N3ZX04Z TEXT:"only just begun"] warming up to activist investors. Some version of Hyundai Motor's (005380.KS) most recent buyback, which targeted both preferred stock and ordinary shares, might be less ambitious — but it's also less likely to land like a bad joke among local investors. Follow Hudson Lockett on Bluesky and X . At the Sohn San Francisco Investment Conference on October 13, Palliser Capital's Chief Investment Officer James Smith called on Samsung Electronics to issue American Depositary Receipts to help pay for the repurchase of $100 billion worth of non-voting preferred shares. The South Korean chipmaker’s preferred shares trade at a 23% discount to its ordinary stock. Foreign investors accounted for 73% of preferred shareholders in Samsung Electronics at the end of June, compared to 46% of common shares, according to the firm. CONTEXT-NEWS

item.title: Tyler Herro helps Bucks get first win of season versus Pacers
item.description: Tyler Herro compiled 23 points, 10 rebounds and seven assists as the Milwaukee Bucks notched the first win of the Taylor Jenkins era, defeating the visiting Indiana Pacers 110-102 on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Tyler Herro compiled 23 points, 10 rebounds and seven assists as the Milwaukee Bucks notched the first win of the Taylor Jenkins era, defeating the visiting Indiana Pacers 110-102 on Monday. Ryan Rollins added 19, Kyle Kuzma had 17 and Kel'el Ware paired 16 points with 14 rebounds as Milwaukee avoided its first 0-4 start to a season since 1976-77, 50 years ago. Tyrese Haliburton posted 22 points and nine assists for Indiana, while Pascal Siakam chalked up 20 points, 13 boards and six assists. The short-handed Pacers, who had only nine standard-contract players available with Andrew Nembhard (neck and back) and Ivica Zubac (left ankle sprain) joining a lengthy injury list, ran out of puff after closing the deficit to 101-98 with 3:54 remaining. Indiana hit its last field goal with 4:29 remaining, missing its last 10 and going 4 of 22 in the fourth quarter, to be outscored 26-17. The Pacers went on a 12-0 spree either side of the first-quarter horn to seize control after they trailed 31-29 after one. The Bucks went cold in the second frame, shooting 8 of 24 from the field, including 3 of 13 from deep. Meanwhile, Indiana knocked down 6 of 11 from 3-point range, led by Haliburton and Aaron Nesmith, winning the quarter 32-19 to storm ahead 61-50 at half-time. Milwaukee pinched the momentum back in the third, despite Haliburton racking up seven assists for the period. The Pacers hit just 2 of 11 from long range for the quarter, while the Bucks countered with 6 of 12 -- spearheaded by Herro, whose 11-point frame came on 3 of 4 from beyond the arc. Milwaukee crept back in front before Haliburton drained a stepback three to restore Indiana's lead, 85-84, with one to play. The Bucks launched the fourth period with a 10-1 rush to move in front, Indiana starting with three turnovers and going without a field goal until Haliburton's three-point play with 7:13 remaining. Milwaukee's advantage was 101-92 before Siakam responded with six straight points. --Field Level Media

item.title: All Blacks coach Rennie excited by return of triple-threat Fainga'anuku
item.description: Having run the rule over more than 50 players during the tour of South Africa, New Zealand coach Dave Rennie will finally get a look at Leicester Fainga'anuku on the season-ending trip to Britain.
item.dc:creator: Ian Ransom
item.content:encoded: Having run the rule over more than 50 players during the tour of South Africa, New Zealand coach Dave Rennie will finally get a look at Leicester Fainga'anuku on the season-ending trip to Britain. Fainga'anuku was named among six loose forwards in the [USN:L6N46C136 TEXT:"All Blacks' squad for next month's Nations Championship"] tests against Scotland, Wales and England, though there is every chance the explosive 27-year-old could be deployed on the wing or in the midfield as the occasion demands. Fainga'anuku missed the first tranche of Nations Championship matches in July and the subsequent four-test tour of South Africa after sustaining a fractured fibula and high ankle sprain playing for the Canterbury Crusaders in Super Rugby Pacific. More recently, his provincial campaign for Tasman wrapped up early with a head-knock and concussion in the final rounds, and he may not be fully fit for the opening test against Scotland in Edinburgh on November 7. Rennie, however, is confident Fainga'anuku can make a difference when his time comes. “It’s less (playing time) than we would have liked,” Rennie told New Zealand media on Tuesday of Fainga'anuku's disrupted buildup. “Still, it’s better to have him in the group for the next four or five weeks. He’s in reasonable nick now.” Having once starred on the wing for the Crusaders, Fainga'anuku made a successful switch to the back row this season. With All Blacks captain Ardie Savea sidelined, along with season-ending injuries to Luke Jacobson and Shannon Frizell, Fainga'anuku takes his place ahead of test loose forward Du’Plessis Kirifi and impressive young flanker Semisi Ta'eiloa. "It gives you massive flexibility," Rennie said of Fainga'anuku's versatility. "You can name a 5-3 bench but it’s generally a 6-2 (split) and he can definitely make (an) impact in all of those spots." Rennie will also have a first look at number eight Christian Lio-Willie, who debuted last year and played three tests under former head coach Scott Robertson. He said there were serious discussions about taking Lio-Willie to South Africa before they opted for other players ahead of him. "He's really tough. He's got a big engine, a really high skill-set and suits the type of game we're trying to play. We’re really excited for him," he said. Still coming back from a calf injury, Richie Mo'unga was included in the tour squad with incumbent flyhalf Damian McKenzie and the uncapped Josh Jacomb. Mo'unga had recovered quicker than hoped from his injury but the elite playmaker is more likely to play in the second test against Wales, rather than come straight back in for Scotland, Rennie said.

item.title: Thunder overcome big injuries to beat Suns for fourth straight win
item.description: Ajay Mitchell scored 30 to lead the Oklahoma City Thunder to a 125-114 home win over the Phoenix Suns a day after the Thunder lost a pair of starters to long-term injuries.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Ajay Mitchell scored 30 to lead the Oklahoma City Thunder to a 125-114 home win over the Phoenix Suns a day after the Thunder lost a pair of starters to long-term injuries. Oklahoma City was playing its first game since Jalen Williams suffered a fractured fibula and a dislocated left ankle in the closing minutes of the Thunder's win over the Clippers. Earlier in that game, Cason Wallace suffered a torn labrum. Both will require surgery and will be out long term. But even without those two and Chet Holmgren, who missed the second night of a back-to-back, Oklahoma City had plenty of firepower to outlast the Suns and win their fourth consecutive game to start the season. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scored 26 points on 11-of-18 shooting, Jared McCain added 18, and Isaiah Hartenstein had 15 points and 13 rebounds. Aday Mara had 11 points and 11 rebounds for his first career double-double. The game might have been another costly one for the already-thin Thunder though. Alex Caruso left the game late in the second quarter after turning his right ankle. While Oklahoma City's star came up big, Phoenix's Devin Booker struggled. Booker had scored a combined 66 points over the first two games of the season but finished with just three points on 1-of-7 shooting. It was Booker's lowest-scoring game since Christmas 2022 when he left due to injury less than five minutes into the game. Other than that, Booker hadn't been held to fewer than five points since his rookie season of 2015-16. Jalen Green led the Suns with 20 points while Dillon Brooks added 19. Though the Thunder trailed for only a few seconds in the game, it wasn't until late in the second quarter when they took control. Oklahoma City scored on nine of 11 possessions during its 22-6 run. The Thunder scored a pair of second-chance buckets during the stretch including a McCain 3-pointer. The Suns have struggled early in the season to limit opponents' offensive rebounds. Gilgeous-Alexander picked up his fifth foul with more than three minutes remaining in the third quarter and headed to the bench. But the Suns could only cut the deficit from 16 to 14 without the two-time Most Valuable Player on the floor for the rest of the quarter. Oklahoma City then reeled off a 12-2 run early in the fourth to put the game away. --Field Level Media

item.title: Rupee's oil-linked losses meet key hurdle, RBI defence in focus
item.description: Rising oil prices continue to weigh on the outlook for the Indian rupee, with traders watching for support near a key technical level and the response of the central bank.
item.dc:creator: Nimesh Vora
item.content:encoded: Rising oil prices continue to weigh on the outlook for the Indian rupee, with traders watching for support near a key technical level and the response of the central bank. The rupee is expected to open flat to marginally weaker on Tuesday, having dropped 0.3% in the previous session to 95.1850 to the dollar. Brent crude is hovering near $115 a barrel, a six-month high, with little relief in sight. Analysts see limited scope for an immediate pullback, with renewed attacks by Iran-aligned Houthis on Saudi Arabia, a key oil producer, raising concerns over supply disruptions. The Indian currency's recovery towards 94.30 last week, driven largely by central bank intervention and one-off inflows, is being tested by a lack of macroeconomic support. Portfolio flows remain weak, while fragile sentiment towards the rupee is encouraging companies to step up hedging, adding to the currency's vulnerabilities. The rupee came under sustained pressure on Monday despite signs of RBI dollar selling, underscoring the challenge facing the central bank. Traders see 95.30 as a key level to watch, given the RBI's more aggressive intervention around that level. A sustained break could expose the rupee to a deeper decline towards 96 per dollar, they said. "It increasingly looks like the RBI will allow the rupee to weaken at a measured pace, having supported the currency around the 95-per-dollar level for a while," a currency trader at a private-sector bank said. ASIAN CUES Asian currencies were mixed ahead of the Federal Reserve's policy decision on Wednesday, offering little direction to the rupee. While risk appetite was relatively firmer across the region, traders said that has done little to support the rupee, with domestic flows and oil prices remaining the dominant drivers.

item.title: Ex-BOJ chief Kuroda backs more rate hikes, his former deputy urges caution
item.description: The Bank of Japan will likely consider raising interest rates at each upcoming meeting, according to a new book by former bank chief Haruhiko Kuroda, who supported his successor's current push to unwind a decade of extremely loose monetary policy.
item.dc:creator: Leika Kihara
item.content:encoded: The Bank of Japan will likely consider raising interest rates at each upcoming meeting, according to a new book by former bank chief Haruhiko Kuroda, who supported his successor's current push to unwind a decade of extremely loose monetary policy. Kuroda's views contrast with those of his former deputy Masazumi Wakatabe, whose book published in September warned against premature rate hikes and urged policymakers to stay focused on boosting demand. The remarks show a divergence in policy thinking between Kuroda, who took part in the monetary leg of former premier Shinzo Abe's "Abenomics" reflationist policies, and Wakatabe who, together with Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, focuses on preserving the legacies of Abenomics. While raising interest rates too hastily could cause economic stagnation, moving too slowly could prevent incumbent governor Kazuo Ueda from completing policy normalisation, Kuroda said. "I'm sure the BOJ will examine whether to raise interest rates by 25 basis point at each policy meeting to bring them close to levels deemed neutral to the economy," he said in the book published this month, which looked back at his decade at the helm at the BOJ. Wakatabe, however, believes there are other priorities currently for monetary policy. "Real economic growth remains low and while Japan is experiencing inflation, half of the price rises are driven by cost-push factors," Wakatabe said in his book, published in September, on Takaichi's economic policies. Wakatabe is known as a reflationist with close ties to Takaichi and currently serves as a member of a key government economic panel. WAKATABE URGES CAUTION Kuroda deployed a radical stimulus programme in 2013 with a pledge to fire up inflation to the BOJ's 2% target in two years. But the target proved elusive, forcing the BOJ to maintain ultra-loose policy throughout his term that ended in 2023. Ueda steered an exit from Kuroda's stimulus in 2024, as a tight job market and rising raw material costs from the Ukraine war lifted consumer inflation. The BOJ has raised rates several times, including in September to a 31-year high of 1.25%, and is expected to declare victory on [USN:L3N46C02N TEXT:"Friday"] in its 14-year battle to meet its price target. In his book, Kuroda said he sought to eradicate Japan's deflationary mindset with simple communication, and "cut off his escape route" by setting a timeframe for hitting the price goal at the risk of depriving the BOJ of policy flexibility. He said he became convinced Japan had fully emerged from deflation around 2024 as wages began to rise. Wakatabe served as deputy BOJ governor from 2018 to 2023. He is seen as among candidates to succeed Ueda when his term ends in 2028, if Takaichi were to stay on as premier long enough to hand-pick the next BOJ chief. "The BOJ would need to do quite some explaining if it were to raise rates when real economic growth is negative and price rises are driven mostly by cost-push factors," Wakatabe wrote in his book. A rate hike may become possible if Takaichi's spending plans and growth strategies stimulate investment and fund demand, thereby pushing up Japan's neutral rate, he said.

item.title: Bond market is a buy right now, JP Morgan Asset Management's fixed income head says
item.description: There is a "generational amount of yield" in bond markets and it is time to buy debt, with a return of as much as 8% on offer in the US over the next the year, Bob Michele, J.P. Morgan Asset Management's head of global fixed income, said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: There is a "generational amount of yield" in bond markets and it is time to buy debt, with a return of as much as 8% on offer in the US over the next the year, Bob Michele, J.P. Morgan Asset Management's head of global fixed income, said on Tuesday. The bond market has rebounded following a selloff this month and last, especially in developed-market sovereign debt: "We expect both the Fed funds rate and the Treasury curve to converge (around 4.5%)," Michele told reporters in Singapore "Generally at the end of a hiking cycle the yield curve is flat ... so there's plenty of room for yields to run from where they are," he said Carry and price appreciation are likely to deliver a return in the US market of 7% to 8% over the next 12 months, he said US 10-year yields were around 4.99% on Tuesday having spent much of the past few weeks above 5% Investors expect the Fed funds rate window to stay at 3.75% to 4% when the Federal Reserve announces its interest rate decision on Wednesday "There is yield all over the place," said Michele. "When we looked at the Treasury curve a few weeks ago when it first went above 5%, to us the buy signal was real yield in the US that got to 3%. The last time we saw that was 2002. So at close to 25 years, that's a buying opportunity." Japan, Australia, investment-grade credit and emerging market sovereign debt are among the stronger picks, he said. "Everyone senses there's a generational amount of yield in bond markets," he said. "It's pretty clear with the global capex cycle out there, recession is a very low probability. That means every backup in credit spread (you) should buy." The "tail risk," he said, was the Fed needing to hike much further than 4.5% to contain inflation

item.title: Singapore foreign minister heads to Indonesia amid tensions over gas and haze
item.description: Indonesia will host Singapore's top diplomat on Tuesday, its foreign ministry said, as tensions simmer between the two neighbours over persistent haze from Indonesia's wildfires and Jakarta's decision to cut gas supplies to the city-state.
item.dc:creator: Xinghui Kok, Fransiska Nangoy
item.content:encoded: Indonesia will host Singapore's top diplomat on Tuesday, its foreign ministry said, as tensions simmer between the two neighbours over persistent [USN:L6N45Z09S TEXT:"haze"] from Indonesia's wildfires and Jakarta's decision to cut [USN:L6N46A01Z TEXT:"gas supplies"] to the city-state. Jakarta cut pipelined gas to Singapore by about 8% as of Saturday, saying it was safeguarding domestic supplies. The move came days after Indonesia's energy minister threatened to review [USN:L6N4680QU TEXT:"export contracts"] with countries "that are not cooperative and do not treat Indonesia with mutual respect". He did not name the countries. The visit by Singapore Foreign Minister Vivian Balakrishnan, which Singapore has yet to confirm, comes as frustration builds in the city-state and neighbouring Malaysia over transboundary haze from Indonesia's [USN:L6N4610CY TEXT:"most intense"] forest fires in 11 years. [USN:L4N45T0LE TEXT:"Singapore generates"] up to 95% of its electricity from natural gas, and though the supply cut from Indonesia amounts to less than 2% of daily demand, Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said on Sunday that he expects contract signatories to "honour their commitments". Indonesia's energy minister, Bahlil Lahadalia, [USN:L6N46C0FK TEXT:"hit back"] on Monday, saying the amount of gas now being supplied to Singapore met the minimum level stipulated under their agreement. "Our nation is a nation that honours contracts, rules. So don't teach Indonesia on how to honour contracts," Bahlil told a press conference, where he outlined details of gas exports to "so-called brothers and sisters". 'THIS ENTIRE REGION IS SUFFERING' Indonesia's fires have raged for months and driven up pollution and respiratory illness across the country, with thick haze also drifting into Singapore, Malaysia and East Timor. Singapore has not directly criticised the Indonesian government over the haze and has offered assistance, but it has sent notices to Indonesian companies it says are responsible for the blazes. Singapore Senior Minister K Shanmugam expressed disappointment last week over remarks made about the haze by an Indonesian official, who said that Indonesia's forests provided Singapore and Malaysia with oxygen. "Frankly, it is not right to say this when this entire region is suffering as a result of the bad behaviour of companies breaching regulations," Shanmugam said. "The people suffering the most are Indonesians themselves." Singapore's state investor Temasek and its sovereign wealth fund GIC were also on the defensive last week, rejecting allegations by a former Indonesian trade minister that they had pressured global index provider MSCI to consider demoting Indonesia's equities to [USN:L6N46208E TEXT:""standalone" market status"]. Indonesia's government has not commented on the allegation by the former minister. Veteran Singaporean diplomat Bilahari Kausikan called the gas cuts an "attempt at intimidation" but said they would be ineffectual. "The cost to Indonesia will far, far outlive any twinge we may feel," he posted on Facebook.

item.title: Cavaliers erase 15-point deficit, hand Timberwolves first loss in OT
item.description: Donovan Mitchell hit a go-ahead midrange jumper with 1:02 remaining in overtime as the host Cleveland Cavaliers rallied from a 15-point deficit to defeat the previously unbeaten Minnesota Timberwolves 127-125 on Monday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Donovan Mitchell hit a go-ahead midrange jumper with 1:02 remaining in overtime as the host Cleveland Cavaliers rallied from a 15-point deficit to defeat the previously unbeaten Minnesota Timberwolves 127-125 on Monday night. Timberwolves superstar Anthony Edwards missed a wide-open 3-pointer with 3.9 seconds remaining that could have tied the game. Peyton Watson grabbed the rebound and made two free throws to push Cleveland's lead to 127-122. Edwards connected on a 3-pointer at the buzzer to finish with a season-high 47 points, his seventh career regular-season game with at least 47. The Timberwolves had won their first three contests by 20-plus points. Mitchell finished with 26 points and seven assists, while James Harden had 19 points and nine assists for the Cavaliers, who improved to 2-1. Evan Mobley added 18 points and 10 rebounds, and rookie Meleek Thomas scored 16 off the bench in his NBA debut. Jaden McDaniels had 14 points and Rudy Gobert collected 20 rebounds and five points, but missed all nine of his field goal attempts for the Timberwolves. LaMelo Ball had 11 points and seven turnovers. Edwards scored on consecutive possessions to give Minnesota a 108-104 lead with 1:45 remaining, but Harden's floater with 10 seconds left tied the game at 113. Watson, who finished with 15 points and eight rebounds, then blocked Edwards' attempt in the closing seconds to force overtime. The game featured four ties and 12 lead changes in the final 16 1/2 minutes. Cleveland used a 12-0 run midway through the third, fueled by eight points from Harden, to seize a 70-69 lead. It began a wild stretch that saw nine lead changes and two ties in the final 4 1/2 minutes of the period, ending in an 86-86 deadlock. The Timberwolves carried a 60-50 lead into the half, with Edwards pouring in 20 points, including a drive that gave them their largest lead, 54-39. Ball had nine points and Gobert grabbed eight rebounds, while Thomas had 10 to pace Cleveland. Edwards had 11 points and McDaniels added nine in the first as Minnesota seized a 29-16 lead. Thomas had eight points in six minutes, allowing the Cavaliers to trim their deficit to 31-24 after one. Edwards was listed as questionable due to right-knee injury management, but Minnesota coach Chris Finch said the team was evaluating it daily and did not consider it a long-term concern. The Timberwolves played their initial back-to-back set of the season after beating the Toronto Raptors 117-94 at home Sunday. --Field Level Media

item.title: Cooper Flagg returns to put up 29 as Mavericks keep Heat winless
item.description: Reigning Rookie of the Year Cooper Flagg returned from a one-game absence to score 29 points and dish 11 assists as the visiting Dallas Mavericks defeated the Miami Heat 113-109 on Monday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Reigning Rookie of the Year Cooper Flagg returned from a one-game absence to score 29 points and dish 11 assists as the visiting Dallas Mavericks defeated the Miami Heat 113-109 on Monday night. Giannis Antetokounmpo posted his first triple-double for the Heat -- 29 points, 15 rebounds and 11 assists -- but Miami fell to 0-4 on the season. Flagg, who sat out Saturday due to a left shoulder injury, added six rebounds against the Heat. He shot 12-for-23 overall and 2-for-8 on 3-point attempts. Kyrie Irving, who was rested in Dallas' previous game, posted 18 points, six rebounds and six assists. The Mavericks, who have alternated losses and wins in their four games, got 20 points and nine rebounds from P.J. Washington plus 15 points from reserve Walter Clayton Jr. Mavericks rookie first-round pick Sergio de Larrea, who was coming off a 21-point game, was held scoreless in six minutes off the bench. He left the game in the second quarter because of a right knee strain, and he didn't return. Besides Antetokounmpo's contributions, Miami got 21 points from Davion Mitchell. All-Star center Bam Adebayo was held to eight points and eight rebounds, shooting 3-of-10 from the floor, including 0-for-5 from 3-point range. Andrew Wiggins had a 3-point attempt with 31.1 seconds left that would have put the Heat on top, but the shot missed. Following a timeout, Flagg drove for a layup with 10 seconds left that made it a four-point margin. Miami didn't lead until Tim Hardaway Jr. made a 3-pointer with 1:50 left in the first quarter. By the end of the period, the Heat were up 27-23 thanks to 52.4% shooting as compared to 29.6% for Dallas. The Heat stretched their second-quarter lead to 12 points, but Dallas went on a 17-4 run to close the half, and the Mavericks led 53-52 at intermission after a late Washington 3-pointer. Daniel Gafford's block of Antetokounmpo's dunk attempt was one of the quarter's highlights. Flagg led all first-half scorers with 13 points. For Miami, Antetokounmpo had 12 points, 10 rebounds and eight assists by the break. Antetokounmpo got even hotter in the third quarter, scoring 13 points as the Heat went up 84-83 by the end of the period. In the fourth, Dallas surged ahead 104-97 on a Flagg three-point play with 4:52 remaining, forcing Miami to call timeout. However, the Heat could not rally, extending their losing streak. --Field Level Media

item.title: Payton Pritchard ignites Celtics offense in win over Bulls
item.description: Payton Pritchard came off the bench to score a game-high 28 points to lead the Boston Celtics to a 134-99 victory over the visiting Chicago Bulls on Monday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Payton Pritchard came off the bench to score a game-high 28 points to lead the Boston Celtics to a 134-99 victory over the visiting Chicago Bulls on Monday night. Pritchard made 7-of-10 shots from behind the 3-point arc. Jayson Tatum added 23 points, seven rebounds and six assists for Boston, which made 21 of its 44 3-point attempts and had a 54-40 edge in rebounds. Norman Powell led the Bulls with 20 points. Caleb Wilson tossed in 17, and Josh Giddey and Matas Buzelis each finished with 11. Leonard Miller had nine points and nine rebounds. Chicago was 33 of 84 from the field (39.2%). Each team committed 25 turnovers. Boston led 33-21 after one quarter, and had its largest lead in the first half, 44-28, with 9:12 left in the second quarter. Miller made a layup to cap a 12-0 run that cut Boston's lead to 44-40, but an 8-1 spurt put the Celtics up 54-44 with 3:27 remaining in the half. Boston led 66-54 at halftime. Tatum had 19 points, six rebounds and five assists in the first half. The Bulls were 18 of 46 from the field (39.1%) through the first two quarters. The Bulls were within seven points early in the second half, but Boston began to take control midway through the third quarter. An 11-1 run handed Boston a 95-71 lead, and three straight Pritchard 3-pointers extended Boston's advantage to 104-73 with 43.6 seconds remaining in the third. Boston led 105-75 after three quarters. Pritchard tossed in 19 points in the third, and he did most of his damage when Tatum was on the bench with foul trouble. The Celtics had a 112-80 lead following a Mike Conley 3-pointer with 8:36 to play, and led by as many as 40 points in the final quarter. --Field Level Media

item.title: Indian shares muted as oil stays near 6-month high, Fed rate decision in focus
item.description: Indian shares were little changed on Tuesday, pausing after previous session's gains, as oil remained near $115 a barrel and investors stayed cautious ahead of the US Federal Reserve's policy decision later this week.
item.dc:creator: Bharath Rajeswaran, Vivek M
item.content:encoded: Indian shares were little changed on Tuesday, pausing after previous session's gains, as oil remained near $115 a barrel and investors stayed cautious ahead of the US Federal Reserve's policy decision later this week. The benchmark Nifty 50 (.NSEI) fell 0.06% to 22,738.55, and the Sensex (.BSESN) shed 0.16% to 73,497.28, as of 09:49 a.m. IST. Twelve of the 16 major sectors logged gains. The broader small-caps (.NIFSMCP100) and mid-caps (.NIFMDCP100) rose 1.7% and 0.5%, respectively. Brent crude futures hovered near a six-month high after attacks on Saudi Arabia dampened hopes of an immediate easing of regional tensions. Higher oil prices hurt India, which imports most of its energy needs, as they can raise inflation, strain its fiscal deficit, and hit corporate profits. "Domestic markets are likely to be subdued as continued attacks on Saudi Arabia keep concerns over potential supply disruptions and inflation elevated," said Siddhartha Khemka, head of wealth management research at Motilal Oswal Financial Services. "Equities could remain muted until greater clarity emerges on the Middle East situation and central bank policy decisions." The Fed is expected to hold interest rates steady on Wednesday before resuming its tightening cycle with a December increase, according to a Reuters [USN:L6N46606V TEXT:"poll"] of economists. IT index (.NIFTYIT) fell 1.8%. Infosys (INFY.NS) fell 2.8%, reversing the 1.1% rise in the previous session. The country's No. 2 software services firm by revenue lowered its revenue growth guidance for fiscal 2027 after reporting higher-than-expected September-quarter revenue after market hours on Friday. [USN:L3N46C0SM TEXT:"Tata Consumer Products"] (TACN.NS) rose 5.9% after reporting better-than-expected second-quarter profit, helped by steady demand for its packaged foods and beverages as the company expands beyond traditional tea and salt businesses. Sona BLW (SONB.NS) jumped 6.3% after posting a year-on-year rise in the September quarter revenue and profit. Astec Lifesciences (ASTE.NS) lost 2.5% after reporting a decline in quarterly profit.

item.title: Australia's AirTrunk bags $3 billion green loan to expand Sydney data centre
item.description: Blackstone-backed AirTrunk secured a A$4.25 billion ($2.98 billion) green loan to fund the continued development of its SYD3 campus in Western Sydney, supporting the expansion of digital infrastructure in the region.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Blackstone-backed (BX.N) AirTrunk secured a A$4.25 billion ($2.98 billion) green loan to fund the continued development of its SYD3 campus in Western Sydney, supporting the expansion of digital infrastructure in the region. Here are some details: Sydney-headquartered AirTrunk said the project, one of Australia's largest hyperscale data centres, will add secure and resilient infrastructure for cloud computing, AI and other digital services used by Australian businesses, governments and communities A consortium of 32 local and international financial institutions backed the green loan, making it one of the largest lending groups assembled for a data centre financing in Australia, the company said The green loan was underwritten by 14 lead banks, including DBS Bank (DBSM.SI) , MUFG Bank (8306.T) , National Australia Bank (NAB.AX) , HSBC (HSBA.L) and UOB (UOBH.SI) , the data centre operator said Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation (8316.T) , HSBC and UOB acted as green loan coordinators, it added The green loan brings AirTrunk's total committed debt financing to about A$38.4 billion globally, including more than A$19.8 billion across its Australian projects Construction of the expanded SYD3 development is expected to be completed by mid-2028, and the project is likely to support more than 10,000 jobs across construction, trades, engineering, logistics and safety The financing comes despite growing investor caution around capital-intensive AI infrastructure projects AirTrunk's announcement comes as Australian data centre operator NextDC (NXT.AX) [USN:L4N4661TS TEXT:"last week said"] it would shelve all new development projects and land acquisitions for the foreseeable future and trimmed its revenue forecasts Firmus, another Australian data centre operator backed by Nvidia (NVDA.O) , [USN:L1N45U12T TEXT:"shelved its $5 billion IPO plan"] earlier this month as credit investors become increasingly selective toward AI-linked companies ($1 = 1.4249 Australian dollars)

item.title: Jay-Z to headline next year's Super Bowl halftime show
item.description: Jay-Z will headline the 2027 Super Bowl halftime show in February, the National Football League announced on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Jay-Z will headline the 2027 Super Bowl halftime show in February, the National Football League announced on Monday. The show at the NFL championship game is the most-coveted showcase in the world of music. US television ratings for the halftime performance often top 100 million viewers and rank higher than the audience for the game itself. Iconic artists including the Rolling Stones, Beyonce, Madonna, Prince and Bruce Springsteen have taken the Super Bowl stage over the years. Puerto Rican rapper Bad Bunny headlined the show at the last Super Bowl. Next year's Super Bowl will take place on February 14 in Los Angeles. It will be broadcast on Walt Disney's ABC and ESPN television networks and will stream on Disney+ and the ESPN app. Jay-Z's company Roc Nation has produced the Super Bowl halftime show since 2019, and he plays a key role in selecting each year's performer. "For several years, we've had the privilege of working closely with Jay-Z and Roc Nation, and I've seen the extraordinary impact he has had on the Super Bowl Halftime Show," NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell said in a statement. "When we first reached an agreement with Roc Nation to produce the show, I had just one request: that Jay-Z take the stage himself one day, whenever the moment felt right to him." Jay-Z is known for hits such as "99 Problems" and "Hard Knock Life." The 56-year-old rapper has also collaborated with artists including Alicia Keys on "Empire State of Mind" and his wife, Beyonce, on "Crazy in Love".

item.title: Bank of Korea warns country's chip exports could fall by up to $100 billion if AI spending slows
item.description: South Korea's semiconductor exports could fall by $50 billion to $100 billion compared with earlier forecasts if capital spending on artificial intelligence by major US technology firms slows next year, according to central bank data.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: South Korea's semiconductor exports could fall by $50 billion to $100 billion compared with earlier forecasts if capital spending on artificial intelligence by major US technology firms slows next year, according to central bank data. In a written response submitted to lawmaker Ahn Do-geol, the Bank of Korea (BOK) modelled a "pessimistic scenario" to assess the economic fallout if US tech giants curb their aggressive infrastructure outlays. Under the scenario, a sudden export shortfall would shave approximately 0.4 percentage point off South Korea's gross domestic product (GDP) growth rate next year, by driving the country's current account surplus well below the central bank's initial projection of $430 billion for 2027. The scenario assumed a 10% decline in Korean semiconductor unit prices. The assessment underscores growing anxiety over South Korea's heavy reliance on chips, which account for roughly half of its exports. The report said combined capital expenditure by five major US technology firms, Amazon, Google, Microsoft, Meta, and Oracle, has been growing rapidly, from $40 billion last year to an estimated $80 billion this year, and is projected to reach $110 billion next year. However, the BOK cautioned that considerable uncertainty remains over the trajectory of AI demand and the broader memory chip business cycle.

item.title: Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted Houthi missiles, drones attacking kingdom
item.description: The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen said on Tuesday it intercepted and destroyed ballistic missiles and drones launched by the Houthis towards two regions of Saudi Arabia, as the conflict between the kingdom and the Iran-aligned group intensifies.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen said on Tuesday it intercepted and destroyed ballistic missiles and drones launched by the Houthis towards two regions of Saudi Arabia, as the conflict between the kingdom and the Iran-aligned group intensifies. The Houthis launched three ballistic missiles towards Saudi Arabia's Eastern Region, and four drones towards the country's Southern Region, the coalition said. Saudi Civil Defense issued early warning alerts for a potential hostile threat in the Eastern Region and in Kharj governorate, later saying the danger had passed in both areas. Saudi Arabia has intensified its strikes on the Houthis since the group captured strategic areas along Yemen's Red Sea coast last month, advancing towards [USN:L8N4520BL TEXT:"the Bab el-Mandeb Strait"], a key global shipping route for Gulf oil producers on the other side of the Arabian Peninsula from the Strait of Hormuz. The renewed fighting between the two sides has shattered a 2022 UN-brokered truce that largely halted attacks between the Saudi-led coalition, which backs Yemen's internationally recognised government, and [USN:L1N45Q02Z TEXT:"the Houthis"], who control the capital Sanaa. The escalation has also opened another front in the US-Israeli war on Iran .

item.title: Drew Doughty, Kings end Rangers' home-ice winning streak
item.description: Drew Doughty collected a goal and two assists on Monday for the visiting Los Angeles Kings, who scored three times in the first period and earned a 6-3 victory over the New York Rangers.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Drew Doughty collected a goal and two assists on Monday for the visiting Los Angeles Kings, who scored three times in the first period and earned a 6-3 victory over the New York Rangers. The result snapped New York's season-opening six-game home winning streak. Taylor Ward scored 1:15 into his season debut and Brandt Clarke also tallied as the Kings took a two-goal lead in the opening 4:52 by scoring on their first two shots against new Rangers goalie James Reimer. Doughty scored his first goal in 25 regular-season games as the Kings won for the third time in four games and earned their sixth straight win over New York.
