Former Ranger Artemi Panarin had the secondary assist on Doughty's first-period tally before scoring a power-play goal 90 seconds into the second period. Los Angeles' Mikey Anderson also scored in the second and Joel Edmundson capped it with an empty-net goal. Alex Laferriere contributed two assists as 12 players recorded a point for the Kings. Los Angeles goalie Darcy Kuemper made 23 saves. Reimer allowed three goals on eight shots in his debut for his ninth team. He tied Cam Talbot's NHL record for the most teams by a goalie. Dylan Garand relieved Reimer and allowed two goals on 17 shots. J.T. Miller scored in the first period, Adam Fox had a power-play tally in the second and Tye Kartye tallied in the third for the Rangers, who fell to 1-4-1 in their past six games and have allowed 18 goals during a three-game skid. Kartye added an assist. Los Angeles went ahead when Doughty spotted Ward cutting through the neutral zone. Ward split defensemen Sean Durzi and Marcus Pettersson and finished off a breakaway. During a long stretch of possession in the offensive zone on a delayed penalty drawn by Joel Armia, the Kings doubled the lead when Clarke went to the right edge of the crease and deflected a cross-ice pass from Scott Laughton into the net. After Miller deflected Kartye's pass with his left skate into an open net with 6:59 left in the opening period, Doughty made it 3-1 with a long drive from the left point 4 1/2 minutes later. Panarin's shot from the right circle went off Garand 14 seconds into a power play, and Anderson's goal off a faceoff 6:54 into the second opened a 5-1 lead. --Field Level Media

item.title: Yen slips ahead of central bank bonanza, dollar firms on tech rebound
item.description: The Japanese yen eased against the US dollar on Tuesday, further eroding last week's safe-haven gains, underpinned by a risk-on mood and a weaker euro ahead of key central bank meetings this week that will influence the global rates outlook.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Japanese yen eased against the US dollar on Tuesday, further eroding last week's safe-haven gains, underpinned by a risk-on mood and a weaker euro ahead of key central bank meetings this week that will influence the global rates outlook. The yen was 0.16% weaker at 157.73 per dollar, inching further away from the one-month high it touched last week ahead of the Bank of Japan policy decision later this week. The yen had lost ground on Monday too. The BOJ is set to keep interest rates steady at 1.25% in a [USN:L3N46C02N TEXT:"two-day meeting"] concluding on Friday, but signal its readiness to continue raising borrowing costs on mounting price pressures. A key gauge of Japan's service-sector inflation [USN:L3N46D002 TEXT:"rose"] 3.7% in September from a year earlier, data showed on Tuesday, a sign of increasing price pressures that will likely keep the central bank on track for further interest rate hikes. "We expect the BOJ will conclude that the underlying rate of consumer price inflation is at a level generally consistent with the 2% price stability target," analysts at MUFG said in a note. However, simply touching the target once is not enough, the analysts said, adding that the BOJ will now shift from a focus on the downside risks to inflation to a stance of monitoring risks in both directions. The yen was among the best-performing major currencies last week, as AI jitters in the equity market spurred a haven rush into the currency. Markets price slightly better-than-even odds of a December BOJ hike, so there is plenty of room for a rebound in the yen should Governor Ueda strike a hawkish note, said Ebury analysts in a note. "We still favour another hike at the last meeting of the year, though whether the BOJ will be prepared to commit to that just yet is unclear." Apart from the BOJ, four other major central banks will announce policy decisions this week. The BOJ's meeting follows that of the Fed, which is seen skipping a hike at its two-day meeting concluding on Wednesday. The European Central Bank is also set to keep rates unchanged at 2.5% on Thursday. New Zealand's and Canada's central banks are expected to raise rates this week. DOLLAR FIRMS ON RISK-APPETITE REVIVAL The dollar index held steady near a one-week high on Tuesday at 102.04 as a tech-led rebound on Wall Street revived appetite for risk, while investors await megacap earnings and the US midterm elections. Risk appetite returned overnight after Anthropic's IPO filing and Meta's (META.O) $95 billion equity plan rekindled the artificial intelligence trade. The dollar was also underpinned by a weaker euro , which fell to a near two-week low against the greenback as worries over France's fiscal health piled pressure on the single currency. The euro last fetched $1.1165, down about 1.4% this month. A selloff in French government bonds that drove the country's debt-risk premium to its highest since the 2011 sovereign debt crisis has rekindled concerns about financial stress across the euro zone. The Brazilian real stabilised after it fell sharply against the US dollar after President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva [USN:L2N46B01X TEXT:"won"] a historic fourth term on Sunday against Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, the eldest son of former President Jair Bolsonaro.

item.title: Brandon Miller scores career-high 39 as Hornets beat Wizards
item.description: Brandon Miller scored a career-high 39 points and the Charlotte Hornets held off the visiting Washington Wizards for Monday night's 110-103 victory for their first back-to-back wins of the young season.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Brandon Miller scored a career-high 39 points and the Charlotte Hornets held off the visiting Washington Wizards for Monday night's 110-103 victory for their first back-to-back wins of the young season. Miller made 15 of 28 shots from the field, including five 3-pointers. Naz Reid added 18 points and 12 rebounds for Charlotte, while Grayson Allen scored 15 off the bench, including seven from the free-throw line. Moussa Diabate chipped in 11 points and 17 rebounds. Anthony Davis scored 29 points and grabbed 10 rebounds for the Wizards, hitting three of Washington's nine 3-point attempts. Trae Young added 22 points and 10 assists, Kyshawn George posted 20 points and Alex Sarr had 12 points. The Wizards lost the battle on the boards, especially as the Hornets grabbed 20 offensive rebounds. Miller had horrid shooting outings in the first two games of the season and now he has eclipsed the 30-point mark in consecutive games. Miller's previous career high was 38 points against the Detroit Pistons on Nov. 21, 2024. Charlotte stormed to a 54-44 halftime lead despite a sluggish start to the final game of a three-game homestand. The Hornets carried a 12-point lead into the fourth quarter before Washington mounted a late comeback, getting as close as 103-100. Young went 10 of 20 from the field but attempted only one free throw. The teams combined for 32 free-throw attempts. The Hornets were whistled for only 15 fouls. The Wizards received only 17 points from their reserves. The start of the game didn't suggest the Hornets would have a big night offensively. Washington led 21-19 at the end of the first quarter, while Charlotte shot 33.3% from the field and went 1-for-11 from 3-point range. The Hornets played again without injured Kon Knueppel, Coby White and Grant Williams. --Field Level Media

item.title: Russia, Ukraine begin localised ceasefire to allow for humanitarian operation in Oleshky
item.description: Russia and Ukraine have started a localised ceasefire to allow for a humanitarian operation to begin in the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky, both sides said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Russia and Ukraine have started a localised ceasefire to allow for a humanitarian operation to begin in the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky, both sides said on Tuesday. Russia's defence ministry said on Telegram it stopped shelling in the direction of the Ukrainian city of Kherson from 4 a.m. Moscow time (0100 GMT) to prepare for the humanitarian operation in Oleshky, just across the Dnipro River from Kherson. Dmytro Lubinets, Ukraine's parliament commissioner for human rights, confirmed in a Facebook post the ceasefire has started at the same time. "As head of the Ukrainian negotiating team, I confirm that the Ukrainian side is honoring its commitments," he wrote. Russia and Ukraine have [USN:L1N46911P TEXT:"agreed"] to a localised ceasefire around the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky in southern Ukraine, an arrangement that will enable aid deliveries and allow evacuations from a frontline town suffering acute shortages of food and medicine. Oleshky [USN:L2N46C0BA TEXT:"lies"] on the eastern bank of the Dnipro in Ukraine's southern region of Kherson, opposite the city of Kherson, which is held by Ukrainian forces. Russian troops seized Oleshky during the first days of their February 2022 invasion and have controlled it ever since. The White House said last week that US first lady Melania Trump helped to secure the Oleshky ceasefire. Elsewhere in Ukraine, a Russian missile [USN:L2N46C0Y8 TEXT:"attack"] on the Ukrainian capital Kyiv on Monday killed at least one person and injured 10, including students at a dormitory, with the attacks [USN:L2N46C0SM TEXT:"also"] killing and injuring people in the cities of Kharkiv and Pavlohrad. New explosions were heard on Tuesday morning in Kyiv, a Reuters witness said.

item.title: China's industrial profit growth picks up amid deepening economic divergence
item.description: China's industrial profits grew at a faster pace in September, though a deepening divergence across the economy weighed on business earnings.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: China's industrial profits grew at a faster pace in September, though a deepening divergence across the economy weighed on business earnings. Profits at industrial firms rose 14.4% from a year earlier last month, quickening from a 4.2% increase in August, data from the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) showed on Tuesday. Profits were up 15.5% in the first nine months of this year, largely unchanged from the 15.7% increase in the January-August period. The sectoral divide remained pronounced, with profits in the computer, communication and other electronic equipment manufacturing category more than doubling over the nine-month period, whereas profits in the furniture manufacturing sector fell by more than half, making it one of the worst performers. Also casting a shadow over the sustainability of profit growth, export-oriented firms are bracing for greater uncertainty as expanding trade surpluses stoke tensions with trading partners, particularly Europe. However, CITIC Bank International's chief China economist, Ding Meng, expressed optimism about the outlook because of the rapid growth in AI-related industries. "This suggests that domestic and external demand generated by the development of the AI supply chain has become a key force supporting industrial profits," he said. "Barring a major reversal in the global AI investment boom, industrial profits are expected to continue growing at a rapid pace." A stronger-than-expected 4.5% expansion in [USN:L1N46501H TEXT:"third-quarter"] GDP put China within reach of its annual growth target of 4.5% to 5.0%, but disparities across different parts of the economy suggest the recovery remains unbalanced, with persistent weakness in some sectors continuing to erode corporate profitability. That pressure has become increasingly visible at the company level. Net profit growth at the world's largest electric vehicle battery maker, CATL (300750.SZ) , [USN:L6N4660TN TEXT:"slowed"] sharply in the past quarter, as intense competition in the EV battery market squeezed margins at a time when China's auto sales were in a downturn. China will continue to leverage macroeconomic policies to support growth, expand domestic demand and optimize supply, said NBS statistician Yu Weining, underscoring a push to replace traditional growth drivers with new ones. Industrial profit figures cover firms with yearly revenue of at least 20 million yuan ($3.0 million) from main operations. ($1 = 6.6702 Chinese yuan)

item.title: Asian stocks surge as Anthropic IPO lifts sentiment ahead of earnings, central banks
item.description: Asian stocks surged on Tuesday as AI bellwether Anthropic's eagerly anticipated IPO filing lifted risk appetite ahead of tech earnings that will be a test for the AI trade, and central bank meetings that will influence near-term interest rates.
item.dc:creator: Ankur Banerjee
item.content:encoded: Asian stocks surged on Tuesday as AI bellwether [USN:L6N46C148 TEXT:"Anthropic's"] eagerly anticipated [USN:L3N46C10M TEXT:"IPO filing"] lifted risk appetite ahead of tech earnings that will be a test for the AI trade, and central bank meetings that will influence near-term interest rates. Claude-owner Anthropic disclosed steep loss and red-hot revenue growth in its filing for a US initial public offering, as investors increasingly dissect the potential payoff from massive AI spending and its profitability. Also boosting sentiment was Meta Platforms' (META.O) plans to raise up to $95 billion in its largest-ever equity fundraising. The currency markets are muted ahead of policy decisions from the [USN:L6N46518P TEXT:"Federal Reserve"], European Central Bank and [USN:L3N46C02N TEXT:"Bank of Japan"], with economists expecting all three to stand pat on interest rates, leaving the focus on comments from policymakers to gauge the rates outlook. In stocks, tech-heavy South Korea's KOSPI (.KS11) gained more than 4% in early trading while Japan's Nikkei (.N225) was 1.9% higher. MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan (.MIAPJ0000PUS) rose 1.2%. Nasdaq futures was up 0.4% after US chip stocks (.SOX) rose 2.8% in overnight trade, clocking its biggest one-day jump in a month. European stock futures dipped 0.23%. More than a third of S&P 500 companies are scheduled to report earnings this week, including hyperscalers Alphabet (GOOGL.O) , Microsoft (MSFT.O) and Amazon.com (AMZN.O) . "Given the increased AI scrutiny of late and circular arrangements, investors will want evidence that demand is broadening beyond these interconnected relationships to support the continued infrastructure expansion," said Anthony Saglimbene, Ameriprise's chief market strategist. "Investors need confidence that aggressive capex spending reflects durable business needs and that profitability will hold up as new infrastructure comes into service," he said. Brent crude futures eased 0.7% to $114.95 a barrel, drifting away from a six-month high as investors weighed the potential for a resolution in the US-Israeli war with Iran, keeping supply fears at bay though sentiment remained fragile. Nick Twidale, chief market strategist at ATFX Global, said supply remains the key concern, and any developments that threaten physical exports could see Brent quickly retest recent highs and potentially push back towards $120. The nearly eight-month-old war has rippled across the Middle East, sending oil prices higher, stoking inflation worries and upending the global interest rates outlook, sharpening the focus on the central bank decisions this week. Fed [USN:L6N46518P TEXT:"policymakers"] have telegraphed they will not raise short-term borrowing costs again this week, but with inflation concerns still front and centre, investors believe a rate-hike pause will not last for long. Traders are pricing in a hike from the Fed in December. "Can we expect (US) growth to hold up in an environment of higher rates?," Geng Ngarmboonanant, head of macro and policy, multi-asset solutions, J.P. Morgan Asset Management, said. "We think yes. We believe the US economy is going to be able to manage through higher interest rates." The yield on the US 10-year Treasury note was steady at 4.992%, staying below 5% which it breached in September as investors scurried to Treasuries for safety during stock market tumult over AI worries. The Japanese yen has been the haven of choice in currency markets and was last at 157.72 per dollar ahead of the BOJ decision on Friday. The Japanese central bank is widely expected to declare victory in a nearly 14-year battle to hit its 2% inflation target on Friday and emphasise the risk that prices could overshoot, signalling the chance of an interest rate hike as soon as December. In commodities, gold eased a touch and was last at $4,013.70 per ounce.

item.title: Macklemore vows to fight until 'last breath' at opening of 'Free Palestine' tour
item.description: American rapper Macklemore vowed to continue to speak out loudly against Israel's war in Gaza at the opening of his "Free Palestine" concert tour organised after he was dropped as the opening act for Ed Sheeran over pro-Palestinian remarks.
item.dc:creator: Padraic Halpin
item.content:encoded: American rapper Macklemore vowed to continue to speak out loudly against Israel's war in Gaza at the opening of his "Free Palestine" concert tour organised after he was dropped as the opening act for Ed Sheeran over pro-Palestinian remarks. The Grammy-winning rapper received a deafening ovation in Dublin, where fans in the overwhelmingly [USN:L1N42309T TEXT:"pro-Palestinian country"] came draped in Palestinian flags, black, red and green football jerseys and keffiyeh scarves being sold by vendors outside. "I am proud to stand here on stage in solidarity with the Palestinian people. We will continue to fight for collective liberation until our last breath," Macklemore said on stage, where he waved a Palestinian flag for much of his set. "Six weeks ago, two words is all that it took," he said, referring to the rallying cry of "Free Palestine" and his criticism of the Israeli government's actions in Gaza and the West Bank at New Jersey's MetLife Stadium that led to [USN:L4N4561KP TEXT:"his removal"] from Sheeran's US tour. "Those two words are so threatening to some people that we'd rather silence those two words than confront what they actually mean... Somehow those words have become more controversial than the suffering that made them necessary." The crowd, who [USN:L6N45G145 TEXT:"snapped up"] the 13,000 tickets for Dublin's 3Arena within minutes, chanted "Free Free Palestine" throughout. "We need a speaker for our time. It has to be somebody like that who can reach out to people. He made it feel so alive and I've come out feeling I want to be part of something," said Siobhan Lyons from Dublin, who attended the concert with her daughter. Irish artists who have spoken out against Israel's actions played in support on Monday, including "Take Me to Church" singer Hozier, rap group Kneecap and Beoga, one of the [USN:L1N4570ZS TEXT:"acts who quit"] Sheeran's tour in solidarity with Macklemore. Palestinian singer Lina Makhoul and Palestinian American DJ Habibeats also performed and pro-Palestine activists such as Game of Thrones actor Liam Cunningham spoke between sets. Sheeran, one of the world's top-selling recording artists, [USN:L6N45C00B TEXT:"said stadium owners"] on the remaining dates threatened to bar any further shows with Macklemore on the bill. Palestinian authorities say more than 74,000 people have been killed in Israel's assault on Gaza , launched after Hamas-led fighters killed about 1,200 people in southern Israel on October 7, 2023. Israeli officials deny their actions in Gaza amount to genocide. The "Free Palestine" tour will continue in Paris and London this week with US dates due to be announced later, Macklemore has said.

item.title: US, dozens of countries warn of Sudan famine risk, urge aid
item.description: Dozens of countries including the US and major European powers said Sudan was experiencing an alarming deterioration in its food security and urged parties to the conflict in the country "to lift all impediments on humanitarian assistance."
item.dc:creator: Kanishka Singh
item.content:encoded: Dozens of countries including the US and major European powers said Sudan was experiencing an alarming deterioration in its food security and urged [USN:L1N45S0CI TEXT:"parties to the conflict"] in the country "to lift all impediments on humanitarian assistance." The countries jointly said that in the face of a potential famine, they were calling on the international community to scale up funding and urging financial institutions to adapt their ongoing programs to the food security situation. "Sudan is experiencing an alarming deterioration in its food security. The risk of famine in the coming months, as warned by the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification, needs urgent action," the joint statement released by the US State Department said. "The parties to the conflict bear primary responsibility for alleviating the suffering of the Sudanese people." Sudan's army has been fighting the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces since April 2023, when the two fell out over issues including how to integrate their forces in a planned transition to civilian rule. In June, the United Nations-backed global hunger monitor, the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification, said 5.1 million people in Sudan faced severe hunger. Farmers have struggled to harvest their crops since the [USN:L6N46918Y TEXT:"civil war"] flared in 2023 and have also recently been [USN:L8N4601TR TEXT:"battling a drought"]. The joint statement urged parties in the conflict to authorize humanitarian operations through all crossline and cross-border routes, including air access into Darfur. It also called on them to "sustain presence and protection of humanitarian personnel" throughout Sudan and refrain from strikes on civilian infrastructure. The statement was signed by the US, Australia, the UK, France, Germany and the European Commissioner for Equality, Preparedness and Crisis Management, among others. The State Department said last month that neither the Sudanese Armed Forces, the Rapid Support Forces paramilitary nor either of their respective leaders "represent legitimate, constitutional governance for Sudan." The war has displaced more than 14 million people and unleashed waves of ethnically driven killings . A UN probe said in July RSF forces carried out mass killings, rapes and forced starvation in a city they besieged and captured last year, as part of an intentional policy [USN:L6N43A0Z7 TEXT:"amounting to genocide"]. Washington [USN:L6N45M0KU TEXT:"has also accused"] the RSF of committing genocide and the army of carrying out war crimes. Both have previously denied abuses.

item.title: Predators aim for back-to-back wins as Isles hone in on details
item.description: The Nashville Predators will try to string together wins in consecutive games for the first time this season on Tuesday when they host the New York Islanders, who are trying to avoid their first two-game pointless streak.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Nashville Predators will try to string together wins in consecutive games for the first time this season on Tuesday when they host the New York Islanders, who are trying to avoid their first two-game pointless streak. Nashville rebounded from a disappointing 3-2 overtime loss in Pittsburgh on Saturday by returning home and whipping the Colorado Avalanche 6-2 on Sunday. The Predators led 5-0 with less than three minutes to go in the second period and went 4-for-7 on the power play. It was the most goals they have scored with the man advantage since getting four against the Carolina Hurricanes on Jan. 7, 2012. Ryan O'Reilly scored two goals and added a pair of assists, while Steven Stamkos netted two goals, giving him a team-high seven on the season. O'Reilly is just behind his linemate with six. Stamkos leads the club with 14 points. O'Reilly and Roman Josi have 12 each, while Filip Forsberg has 11. Forsberg and Josi each recorded three points on Sunday. Predators coach Andrew Brunette said his top players gave "a master class" in playing with the puck. In addition, after complaining previously about having too many passengers on the team, he said win over Colorado demonstrated the team's potential. "This sets up ... kind of the standard we're trying to set here a little bit," Brunette said. "We know we can't get to it every night, but we know we can do it, and we need to bring it a little bit more each night." New York spent Monday in Nashville practicing races to the puck and battles along the boards. Those were a couple of the issues that cost the Islanders on Sunday in a 6-3 loss at Dallas. It was a 3-all game after two periods until the Stars pulled away in the final 20 minutes. "(Sunday) night was not our best," Islanders defenseman Ryan Pulock said. "So, just back to playing our right way. Managing the puck. Getting on the forecheck, all those things that have given us a chance to win games." Pulock, in his 12th NHL season, all with the Islanders, tallied his first point of the season with an assist against the Stars. Bo Horvat leads the team with five goals and 12 points. Defenseman Matthew Schaefer, last season's Calder Memorial Trophy winner as the league's top rookie, scored his second goal of the season on Sunday and ranks second on the team with 10 points. New York coach Peter DeBoer said that Schaefer is playing "at another level" from his breakout debut season. "He's physically stronger," DeBoer said. "He's even more assertive than he was last year. He's got great attention to detail defensively. I think every part of his game is better than it was a year ago, and the scary part is, he's got more levels to go to here." Nashville goalie Juuse Saros (3-2-3, 2.82 goals-against average, .908 save percentage) had Sunday off after making a season-high 34 saves in the overtime loss to the Penguins a day earlier. In 11 career games against the Islanders, the netminder is 9-2-0 with a 2.61 GAA and a .909 save percentage. New York's Ilya Sorokin (5-3-0, 2.26 GAA, .919 save percentage) made 32 saves in Dallas on Sunday but saw his personal three-game winning streak end. In seven games against the Predators, he has a 1-4-1 record with a 3.43 GAA and an .883 save percentage. --Field Level Media

item.title: Blues condemn ‘vile messages of hate’ from protest banners at Vegas game
item.description: The St. Louis Blues on Monday released a statement condemning "vile messages of hate," relating to anti-Israel banners that were present at a recent home game.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The St. Louis Blues on Monday released a statement condemning "vile messages of hate," relating to anti-Israel banners that were present at a recent home game. Protestors on Thursday unfurled banners that read "Free America from Israel" and "Israel kills" during the Blues' 6-2 win over the Vegas Golden Knights. The Blues responded with arena staff and local law enforcement to confiscate the prohibited signage and eject the protestors, then Monday followed up with a statement condemning the messages. "The St. Louis organization -- and I personally -- condemn antisemitic rhetoric in all forms," a statement from chairman Tom Stillman said. "The vile messages of hate briefly displayed at our game last Thursday were unfortunate and unforgivable, and not remotely representative of our fans or our hometown. "Antisemitism has no place in our community, and we will never allow it in our building." --Field Level Media

item.title: China tax crackdown hasn't hurt asset management flow - J.P. Morgan AM
item.description: Beijing's drive to tax offshore income, which is prompting some wealthy Chinese to sell assets abroad, has not hit investor flows into J.P. Morgan's asset management division in Asia, according to its Singapore, Southeast Asia and India head.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Beijing's drive to tax offshore income, which is prompting some wealthy Chinese to sell assets abroad, has not hit investor flows into J.P. Morgan's asset management division in Asia, according to its Singapore, Southeast Asia and India head. "You may have things that happen that will affect those flows. But my general view is these are things that just may be a bump in the road, but the road continues," said Ayaz Ebrahim, J.P. Morgan Asset Management chief executive officer for Singapore, Southeast Asia and India, when asked about China's crackdown in an interview in Singapore. "In terms of what we're seeing in terms of flows, it hasn't really impacted at all. Our flows have been decent and they continue to be decent," he said, without offering numbers. Stockbrokers have cited the crackdown as a reason for falls in Hong Kong's [USN:L4N4601U6 TEXT:"equity market"] and in share prices for Singapore [USN:L2N46C0B3 TEXT:"banks"], which have been beneficiaries of deposits and cash flows from rich customers in China and Southeast Asia. Some of China's richest people are winding down their offshore trusts, [USN:L4N45U04N TEXT:"selling shares"], and even switching nationality as a deadline looms to declare income booked overseas, say wealth advisers, lawyers and others familiar with the matter. Ebrahim, who has nearly four decades in markets, said he asset manager was "clearly focusing" on Asia's wealth boom. "Even if China's growing at 3% – it's creating a lot of money still ... I think this trend is here to stay. Definitely," he said. He said the asset manager, which has $4.6 trillion in assets under management according to its website, had recently opened a two-person trading desk in Singapore and that by the first quarter of next year, headcount would have expanded by 20% to 25% over the years since he moved to Singapore in April 2024.

item.title: China is back in the bull semen market, but only the best will do
item.description: Utopia is one of Australia's best Angus bulls: jet black, muscular, he sires big, fast-growing cattle with superb meat quality.
item.dc:creator: Daphne Zhang, Lewis Jackson
item.content:encoded: Utopia is one of Australia's best Angus bulls: jet black, muscular, he sires big, fast-growing cattle with superb meat quality. On a recent morning at the Total Livestock Genetics facility in Camperdown, two hours west of Melbourne, Utopia mounts a cow and is directed by a handler into a receptacle. The high-value semen is divided into hundreds of plastic straws, each containing millions of sperm cells, enough for an impregnation. Frozen in liquid nitrogen, the straws will be shipped to China, which is back in the bull semen market after a near halt in its cattle genetics trade that blocked imports from top sources including the US, Europe, Canada and Australia and rattled local suppliers enough to birth a market for smuggled sperm and livestock. Now, Australian and Canadian suppliers are ramping up shipments and the United States and Britain could be approved soon, people in the industry say, as China tries to upgrade its scrawny, unproductive herds, raise beef output and dairy profitability, and cut a rising import bill. But the resumption this year has come with a strict quality standard, limiting imports to semen from the best 10% of bulls in the country where it is produced, according to government officials, diplomats and genetics companies. The imports -- the first batch from Australia arrived in April -- and the intensive screening, which has not previously been reported, reflect China's recognition that its own cattle cannot match the genetic quality in countries such as the US and Australia, where bigger animals are growing ever more productive, more than 20 industry participants said. "Historically, Chinese cattle were bred for ploughing fields, and Western breeds for meat and milk production," said Hao Hongman, a manager at bull genetics firm Beijing World Wide Sires. "Now Chinese producers want the best imported semen for their cattle to grow faster, eat less and produce more meat and dairy." UPGRADING THE HERD Imported semen can be used to breed cutting-edge animals or given to local cattle to create offspring that aren't top notch but produce more than their forebears. Beef cattle carcasses in China weigh around 150 kilograms, versus nearly 400 kg in the United States, while Chinese dairy cows produce less milk than the US herd, according to the USDA. Better genetics also mean tastier, better-marbled meat, higher-quality milk, faster growth, and less feed. These traits are becoming even more valuable as a wealthier middle class increasingly prefers prime Angus and Wagyu to the chewier cuts used in traditional stewing and braising. By 2024 Chinese consumers ate almost twice as much beef and 30% more dairy than a decade earlier, Chinese official data show. Imports of beef and products such as cream, cheese and butter have ballooned to $25 billion to $30 billion a year. China's eventual goal is to develop world-leading genetics and shift from importer to exporter, as it has done in industries from automobiles to chicken , industry sources said. That will be difficult, said Marcus Rees, general manager of the Australian arm of ABS Global, the owner of the virile bull Utopia. Even as they supply China with very good genes, firms like ABS will make sure they have a pipeline of better animals coming through, he said. Beijing's agriculture and commerce ministries did not respond to requests for comment. 'NOT A FINE WINE' China declared self-sufficiency in animal genetics a national security priority in 2021, identifying cattle breeding as a critical weak spot. By 2026, the government had invested millions of dollars into local breeding centres, but the genetics still lag Western countries. "Local bull stations have good genes but not the most advanced. High-end Chinese farms demand better genetics," said Rone Lane, the Canadian CEO of Beijing World Wide Sires, which sells to Chinese dairy giants including Yili, Mengniu, Feihe, and New Hope. The gap widened after China halted live animal and semen imports from one nation after another between 2019 and 2025 and curtailed imports of cattle embryos and live animals, according to trade data and industry insiders. Many closures coincided with political confrontations, such as US President Donald Trump's ramping up of a trade war and Beijing's then-frosty relations with Canberra and Ottawa. "Genetics get outdated very quickly," said Ian Lahiffe, an agricultural consultant based in Beijing. "Semen is not a fine wine. It doesn't age well. It's an antique within a year." Some Chinese producers became so desperate during the trade shutdown that they smuggled in semen or live cattle via neighbouring countries including Mongolia, Kazakhstan, and Vietnam, a dozen people in the industry said. "Every day, our customers want to know when they can get US semen, and when the US market will reopen," Lane said. BUSY BULL Semen is still flowing only slowly to China, as an expert panel puts each shipment through a review process lasting more than four months to verify that it meets its top 10% rule, genetic companies and diplomats say. Some shipments have been only partially approved after failing to meet the standard, industry insiders said. In Australia, a Chinese audit team arrived last year to check the facility that houses Utopia, a level of scrutiny shown by few other importers, said ABS's Rees. By the end of August, China had received 92,573 straws of semen worth around $700,000 from Australia and Canada combined, Chinese customs data show, far less than the roughly 10 million straws a year imported in the years before the curbs, but business is growing. ABS Australia expects to ship around 200,000 straws over the coming year containing semen from Wagyu, Angus, Holstein and Jersey bulls -- more than it ships to all other countries combined -- and plans to add two or three more Angus bulls to supply China, Rees said. Industry players say the US, which accounts for around 55% of the half a billion dollars' worth of bull sperm shipped globally each year, will be China's dominant supplier -- as it was before the trade was frozen. Utopia, meanwhile, is keeping busy with his twice-weekly collections. Most of his semen will be injected into Chinese dairy cows so their offspring produce more and better meat, Rees said. "China will take as much as he can make," he said. "It's lucky he has very high libido."

item.title: USTR Greer tells EU that loan to Airbus threatens trade truce on aircraft financing
item.description: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told the European Union on Monday that a lack of information about its record-breaking loan to Airbus threatens a delicate transatlantic trade truce, including on financing large civil aircraft (LCA) projects.
item.dc:creator: David Lawder, David Shepardson
item.content:encoded: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told the European Union on Monday that a lack of information about its record-breaking loan to Airbus (AIR.PA) threatens a delicate transatlantic trade truce, including on financing large civil aircraft (LCA) projects. In a statement, Greer expressed frustration that despite "ongoing requests," his office has received no details about the $3.4 billion loan made in June from the European Investment Bank, the EU's official lending arm. US planemaker Boeing (BA.N) had asked the US government in July to [USN:L8N43N0CN TEXT:"press for transparency"] on the loan, which came amid speculation that Airbus would use the funds to develop a new aircraft model. "This situation injects substantial uncertainty into transatlantic trade in the aerospace sector," Greer said. "It is important this situation is resolved as soon as possible to ensure market-driven production in the aerospace sector and to avoid violation of the terms of our hard-won LCA deal." An Airbus spokesman said the EIB loan "is a standard corporate financing facility, similar to commercially-available loans we've signed in the past. "We are actively engaging with the relevant authorities and are happy to share more information about the loan with governments," the spokesman said in an emailed statement. The loan was also meant to diversify Airbus' funding sources, which was "necessary to manage the complexity of a high-value global production system and supply chain." The US and EU fought a [USN:L6N42J10J TEXT:"protracted 17-year battle"] over alleged aircraft subsidies at the World Trade Organization, with both sides winning partial victories before agreeing to a five-year truce in 2021 that forestalled mutual tariffs on some $11.5 billion worth of trade. The truce was extended in July after the EU parliament approved a broader US trade deal that removed tariffs on US industrial goods in return for a 15% US tariff on most EU goods. US President Donald Trump had threatened higher tariffs unless EU member states met a July 4 deadline for ratifying the deal initially reached in July 2025. A key question for USTR is whether the terms of the EIB loan would be considered a subsidy for Airbus, as the WTO has found in the past on such loans. Boeing did not immediately respond on Monday to requests for comment on Greer's statement. The EIB said in July that it finances thousands of companies every year and denied offering Airbus any unusual support. "This is a normal loan, carrying interest, part of the EIB's overall financing activity," a spokesperson for the lender said. Airbus Chief Financial Officer Thomas Toepfer also told reporters in London in July that the loan had been taken out "completely at market level."

item.title: JYP Entertainment soars 10% on reports of tender offer plan to buy up to half of firm
item.description: South Korean pop music agency JYP Entertainment's shares jumped 10% on Tuesday after Korean media reported Japan's Nexroc Group and related firm SVCV Inc were planning to announce a tender offer to buy up to a 50% stake in the company.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: South Korean pop music agency JYP Entertainment's (035900.KQ) shares jumped 10% on Tuesday after Korean media reported Japan's Nexroc Group and related firm SVCV Inc were planning to announce a tender offer to buy up to a 50% stake in the company. The 50% stake is worth about 700 billion won ($528.04 million) based on JYP's current market capitalisation. JYP said it has not received a tender offer. Nexroc Group was not immediately available to comment. JYP Entertainment, founded by South Korean singer-songwriter and producer Park Jin-young (J.Y. Park), is one of South Korea’s leading K-pop entertainment companies, with its main artists including popular K-pop groups such as TWICE, Stray Kids, ITZY and DAY6. The two companies said in a press release that they are targeting between 25% and 50% of JYP's issued shares, with a tender offer price at a 30% premium to a benchmark share price, Yonhap News Agency and other media said. "The 'pre-tender offer announcement' of JYP Entertainment by NEXROC and SVCV is not typical and could be made illegal by the Korean financial authorities," said Douglas Kim, an independent analyst who writes on Smartkarma. "A company has to launch a tender offer when they have enough financial backing/assets that would allow them to launch a tender offer," he said, adding that allowing such a pre-tender offer "could set a bad precedent in the Korean equity markets." ($1 = 1,325.6500 won)

item.title: Canucks, Ducks set out to reverse recent trajectories
item.description: A pair of teams eager to regain the form they showed when the season began will meet Tuesday when the Anaheim Ducks play host to the Vancouver Canucks.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: A pair of teams eager to regain the form they showed when the season began will meet Tuesday when the Anaheim Ducks play host to the Vancouver Canucks. Anaheim snapped a five-game skid Saturday in the finale of a four-game road trip, while Vancouver heads to California after losing ten straight. Anaheim opened the season with four victories over its first five games to show promise, then went into a funk before earning a 5-4 victory on the road against the Philadelphia Flyers on Saturday. The Ducks overcame an early two-goal deficit to slip past the Flyers as Leo Carlsson scored his team's first goal of the game near the midway point of the second period, then assisted on what became the game-winner when Beckett Sennecke scored with 12:50 remaining. "Way better team game this game," Carlsson said. "Obviously, to go down 2-0, they get a 5-on-3 (power play), it was a little tough. But (we) came back in the game. Pretty good." Carlsson's heroics came against the team that signed him to a five-year, $90 million offer sheet in the offseason. The Ducks matched the surprising sum and refused to bid farewell to their budding star. The team's major investment has paid off with Carlsson's team-best 13 points, 10 of them on assists. In his 11th game this season and 25th of his career, defenseman Tristan Luneau scored a goal and added two assists. "When he has confidence, he's insane," Carlsson said of the 22-year-old Luneau, who was a second-round draft pick in 2022. "He's just got to have the confidence all the time, because he's a great defenseman in this league. He's super fast, strong, can do everything. So excited to see his future." The Canucks won two of their first three games to start the season but have gone 0-9-1 since, including a 4-2 home loss to the Minnesota Wild on Sunday. After three consecutive losses on a short homestand, Vancouver is on a two-game California trip that ends at San Jose on Thursday. Elias Pettersson assisted on a goal by Brock Boeser late Sunday and now has a team-best 13 points, with nine on assists. The Canucks took 10 shots in the opening period to five for the Wild and yet still trailed 1-0 through the first 20 minutes. "We had obviously a really good start to the game," Canucks head coach Manny Malhotra said. "Exactly what we tried to establish early. Spent quite a bit of time in their zone. Got the shots we wanted. Everything but the score was a positive for us coming out of the first, and then weren't able to maintain that in the second." Vancouver had just three shots in the second period and was outshot 29-7 over the final 40 minutes. A trip to Anaheim might be just what Vancouver needs. The Canucks are 13-2-0 against the Ducks over the previous four seasons and have won seven of their last eight at Anaheim since December 2021. --Field Level Media

item.title: Oil eases on Middle East diplomacy hopes, Saudi attacks keep supply worries alive
item.description: Oil prices edged lower on Tuesday as the potential for a resolution in the US-Israeli war on Iran kept supply fears at bay, but Brent stayed close to six-month highs as attacks on Saudi Arabia lowered hopes of immediate stability in the region.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Oil prices edged lower on Tuesday as the potential for a resolution in the US-Israeli war on Iran kept supply fears at bay, but Brent stayed close to six-month highs as attacks on Saudi Arabia lowered hopes of immediate stability in the region. Brent crude futures were down 66 cents, or 0.57%, at $115.15 a barrel as of 0000 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude was down 44 cents, or 0.43%, at $101.32. Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan held talks with Iranian officials in Tehran on Monday aimed at [USN:L2N46C041 TEXT:"easing tensions"] in the Middle East. Saudi Arabia said the visit sought to establish open negotiating channels to "prevent the return of military escalation". The four countries agreed to continue talks with a view to strengthening cooperation in peace and security, Iranian state media reported. Hopes of resolution in the conflict erased some fears of supply disruption, lowering risks and pressuring oil prices. However, losses were limited as scope for peace looked fragile, with [USN:L2N46C045 TEXT:"renewed attacks"] by Iran-aligned Houthis on key producer Saudi Arabia. October has been the worst month for [USN:L1N4690RP TEXT:"attacks"] on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and nearby waterways, according to data compiled by a Washington-based think tank that has tracked maritime security incidents worldwide since 2017. The war has rippled across the Middle East, placing the Strait of Hormuz at the center of the turmoil. The narrow waterway carried around a fifth of the world's energy supplies before the conflict erupted in February. Last week, Brent prices surged to more than $117 a barrel, the highest level since April, after a wave of Iranian attacks on tankers around the strait. Brent prices touched $117 on Monday as well. Elsewhere, [USN:L6N46C0P1 TEXT:"Russian refiners"] are raising diesel production in October after the government granted export quotas following the Kremlin's supply agreement with the US, two industry sources close to the matter said.

item.title: Japan's September corporate services prices rise 3.7% yr/yr
item.description: A key gauge of Japan's service-sector inflation rose 3.7% in September from a year earlier, data showed on Tuesday, a sign of mounting price pressures that will likely keep the central bank on track for further interest rate hikes.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A key gauge of Japan's service-sector inflation rose 3.7% in September from a year earlier, data showed on Tuesday, a sign of mounting price pressures that will likely keep the central bank on track for further interest rate hikes. The year-on-year rise in the services producer price index, which tracks the prices that companies charge each other for services, followed a revised 3.5% gain in August, data from the Bank of Japan showed The data is closely watched by the BOJ for clues on the extent to which companies are passing on rising labour costs to service-related prices The BOJ is set to keep interest rates steady at 1.25% in a [USN:L3N46C02N TEXT:"two-day meeting"] concluding on Friday, but signal its readiness to continue raising borrowing costs on mounting price pressures

item.title: Australia's Star Entertainment swings to profit on cost cuts, stronger casino revenue
item.description: Australian casino operator Star Entertainment swung to a first-quarter profit on Tuesday, underpinned by cost-cutting measures and strong performances at its Sydney and Gold Coast operations.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Australian casino operator Star Entertainment (SGR.AX) swung to a first-quarter profit on Tuesday, underpinned by cost-cutting measures and strong performances at its Sydney and Gold Coast operations. Star posted consolidated earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation of A$12 million ($8.42 million) for the three-month period ended September 30, a turnaround from a loss of A$13 million in the year-ago period Its Sydney and Gold Coast casinos generated more than 98% of first-quarter consolidated revenue, which rose 2% to A$284 million The embattled company said it had A$239 million in cash and cash equivalents, as of September 30, and was continuing operational improvement efforts "We now expect to start building cash reserves in FY27, before non-operating items," Star CEO Bruce Mathieson Jr said in a separate announcement The firm also reiterated that Sydney casino's licence remains [USN:L4N45H07W TEXT:"suspended"] and that the manager's appointment has been extended to June 30, 2027 Shares of the company jumped as much as 17.4% to A$0.135, logging their biggest intraday gain since December 18 ($1 = 1.4249 Australian dollars)

item.title: ATP roundup: Alex de Minaur survives scare in Vienna
item.description: No. 5 seed Alex de Minaur of Australia stormed back from down a set and a break to defeat the Czech Republic's Tomas Machac 1-6, 6-4, 6-3 in opening-round action at the Erste Bank Open on Monday in Vienna, Austria.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: No. 5 seed Alex de Minaur of Australia stormed back from down a set and a break to defeat the Czech Republic's Tomas Machac 1-6, 6-4, 6-3 in opening-round action at the Erste Bank Open on Monday in Vienna, Austria. The 10th-ranked player in the world, de Minaur avoided an upset that could have dashed his hopes of qualifying for the eight-man Nitto ATP Finals at season's end. Down 4-2 in the second set, he rattled off the last four games to take momentum and broke Machac's serve three times in the deciding set. Czech eighth seed Jakub Mensik cruised past Austria's Lukas Neumayer 6-2, 6-2 in 63 minutes, while Learner Tien defeated France's Luca Van Assche 6-3, 6-1. Italians Matteo Berrettini and Luciano Darderi advanced in straight sets, and Great Britain's Arthur Fery was up 5-1 when countryman Jacob Fearnley retired. Swiss Indoors Basel No. 9 seed Casper Ruud outlasted Swiss wild card Dominic Stricker 4-6, 7-5, 6-3 in the first round in Basel, Switzerland. Stricker finished with a 13-12 edge in aces, more winners (37-29) and fewer unforced errors (18-26) but could not break Ruud's serve across the final two sets. German lucky loser Daniel Altmaier staved off Argentine qualifier Juan Manuel Cerundolo 6-7 (5), 7-6 (4), 6-4. Denmark's Holger Rune absorbed 32 aces by France's Quentin Halys and eked out a 6-4, 6-7 (2), 7-6 (5) victory, while Portugal's Nuno Borges and Monaco's Valentin Vacherot won in straight sets. --Field Level Media

item.title: Wild, Mammoth clash for Central Division supremacy
item.description: The top two teams in the Central Division meet Tuesday night when the Minnesota Wild visit the Utah Mammoth in Salt Lake City.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The top two teams in the Central Division meet Tuesday night when the Minnesota Wild visit the Utah Mammoth in Salt Lake City. The first-place Wild will conclude a five-game road trip after sweeping back-to-back games over the weekend, winning 5-1 at the Seattle Kraken on Saturday and 4-2 at the Vancouver Canucks on Sunday. Maxim Shabanov and Kirill Kaprizov each had a goal and an assist as the Wild evened their road trip record at 2-2 with the Sunday win. Former Canuck Quinn Hughes, playing his first game in Vancouver since being traded to Minnesota last December, had a goal and an assist and reached 500 career points, while Calvin Pickard made 15 saves. Minnesota was outshot 10-5 in the first period but compiled a 29-7 advantage over the final 40 minutes. "Vancouver came out really hard, physical, aggressive, kind of took the play to us a little bit," Wild coach John Hynes said. "But I thought the second half of the first period we got ourselves competitively into the game the way we needed to, and I liked how we responded throughout." Kaprizov has 13 goals this season and has recorded at least one point in 11 of 13 games. "I don't want to say it's hot start," Kaprizov said. "It's just so many places where we can do better and play better. It's just early season. Just need to be in shape all the time and keep doing (it the) right way, keep playing right." Hughes also has points in 11 of 13 games. After winning three in a row earlier this month, the Mammoth have alternated wins and losses over their past four games, the latest being a 5-4 overtime win against the visiting Tampa Bay Lightning on Saturday. Dmitri Simashev scored his first two NHL goals Saturday, including the winner at 1:44 of overtime, as Utah rallied from a 4-2 second-period deficit to defeat Tampa Bay. "We (didn't execute) a lot of plays and were a little bit nervous, but were capable of regrouping and finding our game and playing much better in the second half of the game," Utah coach Andre Tourigny said. Kailer Yamamoto, Dylan Guenther and Anders Lee also scored for Utah. Vincent Trocheck recorded two assists, and Karel Vejmelka made 29 saves. Vejmelka bounced back after allowing nine goals on 41 shots in Utah's previous two games. "Really proud of him, really proud for him," Tourigny said. "I think we all know how much he cares and how much the team means to him, so to see him bounce back and come up big in key moments and help us to get the two points was huge." Vejmelka is 8-4-1 with a 2.68 goals-against average and a .911 save percentage in 14 games against the Wild. Minnesota's Jesper Wallstedt allowed five goals in his only prior start against the Mammoth, a loss. Utah took two of three meetings last season. Logan Cooley had two goals and an assist in a 6-2 Mammoth win on Oct. 25, 2025. The Mammoth won 5-2 at home on Feb. 27, with Clayton Keller recording a goal and two assists. Minnesota salvaged the final meeting, winning 5-0 on March 10 behind 25 saves by Filip Gustavsson. --Field Level Media

item.title: Israel election: What happens after polls close?
item.description: Israel holds a parliamentary election on Tuesday, its first since the Hamas attack on October 7, 2023 that shook the country and plunged the Middle East into turmoil.
item.dc:creator: Maayan Lubell
item.content:encoded: Israel holds a parliamentary election on Tuesday, its first since the Hamas attack on October 7, 2023 that shook the country and plunged the Middle East into turmoil. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's hold on power is at stake, with centrist rivals promising to usher in a new era, but it might take time before clear results are known. WHEN WILL WE KNOW WHO WON? It is likely this will be known within a few hours of polls closing, but it could take days or even weeks to become clear. Voting starts at 7 a.m. (0500 GMT) and ends at 10 p.m. (2000 GMT), when Israeli TV channels will air exit polls giving the first indications of the outcome. The election results will then start coming in. A clear picture may emerge quickly but if no party or group of parties has a clear parliamentary majority, it could take much longer. The final tally is expected by October 30 and official election results are formally published a week after the election, on November 4. WHY IS IT SO COMPLICATED? Elections to the 120-seat Knesset are meant to be held every four years but early elections have been frequent. The Knesset seats are allocated by proportional representation to national party lists, with parties needing to pass a threshold of 3.25% of the national vote to secure seats. About a dozen parties are widely thought to have a chance of crossing the threshold, so the final tally and seat allocation will take time. WHAT HAPPENS AFTER THE RESULTS ARE PUBLISHED? After the final tally is in, President Isaac Herzog will consult party leaders on whom they want as prime minister and then tap the candidate he believes has the best chance of forming a government. That nominee has up to 42 days to form a government. No single party in Israel has ever won an outright majority, so governments are formed by a coalition of parties, and negotiations on forming a government often take weeks. Every Knesset seat counts and small parties can have a big impact by becoming kingmakers. If the nominee fails, others can get a chance to try. If no government emerges, another election is called, with the present cabinet staying on as a caretaker government.

item.title: Trump oferece US$1 milhão por denúncias que levem a condenações por fraude eleitoral
item.description: O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, afirmou nesta segunda-feira que os EUA vão conceder US$1 milhão a qualquer pessoa que denunciar uma fraude eleitoral que leve à prisão e condenação, uma semana antes das eleições de meio de mandato, que, segundo as pesquisas, podem se revelar difíceis para o Partido Republicano.
item.dc:creator: Kanishka Singh
item.content:encoded: O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, afirmou nesta segunda-feira que os EUA vão conceder US$1 milhão a qualquer pessoa que denunciar uma fraude eleitoral que leve à prisão e condenação, uma semana antes das eleições de meio de mandato, que, segundo as pesquisas, podem se revelar difíceis para o Partido Republicano. O governo Trump tem adotado uma abordagem cada vez mais agressiva em relação à fiscalização eleitoral, pressionando os Estados a fornecerem dados de registro eleitoral e argumentando que são necessárias medidas mais rigorosas para garantir a confiança do público no processo eleitoral. Críticos, incluindo especialistas na área política, assim como autoridades eleitorais democratas e alguns republicanos, consideram essas medidas uma intromissão excessiva do governo federal. “Qualquer pessoa que denunciar fraude eleitoral nas eleições passadas ou nas próximas eleições de meio de mandato de 2026 receberá US$1.000.000 após a prisão e condenação dos responsáveis pela fraude”, escreveu Trump no Truth Social nesta segunda-feira. Algumas autoridades eleitorais disseram à Reuters que se preparam para uma possível interferência federal nas eleições de meio de mandato. Trump já fez alegações falsas relacionadas às eleições no passado, inclusive ao se recusar a reconhecer sua derrota nas eleições de 2020. Seus apoiadores acabaram invadindo o Capitólio dos EUA em 6 de janeiro de 2021, em uma tentativa frustrada de impedir a certificação dessas eleições pelo Congresso. Atualmente, os republicanos detêm uma maioria estreita na Câmara dos Deputados e no Senado. No entanto, às vésperas das eleições de meio de mandato, nas quais o controle do Congresso está em jogo, a popularidade de Trump permanece baixa devido às preocupações dos eleitores com o alto custo de vida e o aumento dos preços dos combustíveis decorrentes da guerra dos EUA e de Israel contra o Irã.

item.title: Netanyahu's political survival on the line as Israel votes
item.description: Opinion polls show a close race between Netanyahu's Likud party and its right-wing allies and a rival alliance led by Gadi Eisenkot, a former military chief of staff and security hawk with backers on the right and in the centre.
item.dc:creator: Steven Scheer, Pesha Magid
item.content:encoded: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu faces a fight for political survival in Israel's election on Tuesday, with voters weighing his leadership after the 2023 [USN:L8N4680E4 TEXT:"Hamas-led attacks"], wars in Gaza and with Iran, and Israel's deepening international isolation. Yet Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving leader with 19 years in office, remains a formidable survivor, with nationalist politics increasingly entrenched and Israel's fragmented system potentially leaving him best placed to form a government. Opinion polls show a close race between Netanyahu's Likud party and its right-wing allies and a rival alliance led by [USN:L6N46303T TEXT:"Gadi Eisenkot"], a former military chief of staff and security hawk with backers on the right and in the centre. Netanyahu is campaigning on his wartime leadership and his alliance with US President Donald Trump , who has endorsed him and joined Israel in waging war on Iran. Netanyahu said on Sunday that Trump was prepared to act again to “finally” remove the Iranian threat, but only if Netanyahu remained in power. Eisenkot has accused Netanyahu of "relying on a campaign of fear-mongering, lies and threats," and said he was confident Trump would work "in full cooperation with any leader chosen by the people." Netanyahu may again depend on far-right leaders Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich to form a government. Both have faced sanctions from some Western countries that accuse them of inciting violence against Palestinians, while [USN:L8N45T0L1 TEXT:"Ben-Gvir's Jewish Power"] party has gained support in opinion polls. Neither Netanyahu nor Eisenkot has a clear path to power. If neither can form a governing coalition in the 120-seat parliament, Netanyahu could stay on as caretaker until another election is held next year. Polls open from 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. (0500 to 2000 GMT). THE OCTOBER 7 RECKONING The election follows one of Israel's most turbulent periods since its establishment in 1948, shaped by the trauma of the October 7, 2023, Hamas attacks, Israel's subsequent military assault in Gaza and deep domestic divisions over the policies of Netanyahu's right-wing government. For many of Netanyahu's opponents, the election turns on [USN:L8N4680E4 TEXT:"accountability"] for the security failures of October 7, Israel's deadliest day. Mali Hajaj, an Education Ministry employee and Eisenkot supporter, said "the most important thing is the establishment of a national inquiry because that's where our healing will come from." Lisa Tortor said she hoped Netanyahu would go and "they can form a new government and do some of the repairing of the damage that Bibi has done for Jews all over the world and for Israel, and Israel's image." Bibi is Netanyahu's nickname. But Nof Gabay, an 18-year-old Likud supporter, rejected the idea Netanyahu was to blame for October 7 and called him "the right man for the state of Israel." "Netanyahu managed the war in the best possible way," Gabay said. THE WARTIME RECORD Israel flattened much of Gaza in the offensive launched after October 7, when Hamas-led militants killed 1,200 people and took another 251 hostage. Gaza health authorities say Israeli attacks killed 74,000 people. Israel also dealt heavy blows to Iran-backed Hezbollah in Lebanon and traded strikes with Iran before a 12-day aerial campaign against Iranian nuclear sites in 2025 and this year's joint US-Israeli war. Eisenkot has said Israel's next government must prevent Iran from acquiring a military nuclear capability, either by force or through an "arrangement" such as a US-backed diplomatic solution. THE COALITION MATH Like nearly all Jewish-led parties in Israel, Eisenkot opposes the two-state solution that underpinned decades of peace negotiations with the Palestinians. But he has criticised Jewish settler violence against Palestinians in the Israeli-occupied West Bank, which has surged since 2023 and strained Israel's ties with Western states, and opposes Netanyahu's far-right coalition partners Ben-Gvir and Smotrich. In some [USN:L8N45Y0MD TEXT:"bastions of Likud"] support, disenchanted voters have been going door to door to turn voters against Netanyahu. Some have turned away from Netanyahu as he battles corruption charges he denies in a long-running criminal trial. A high turnout among voters from [USN:L8N45Z09Z TEXT:"Israel's Arab minority"], Israeli by citizenship but Palestinian by heritage, could help nudge Israel's complex coalition arithmetic in favour of Eisenkot. Though Eisenkot has ruled out partnering with Arab parties, citing a lack of shared values, analysts see a scenario where they prop up a minority government he leads in order to ensure Netanyahu is removed from office. "My expectation is that we will have only a slight majority either way. No landslide," said Israeli political analyst Amotz Asa-El of the Shalom Hartman Institute.

item.title: UK retail body warns 'dam is starting to break' on price rises
item.description: Britain's main retail trade body warned on Tuesday that shops are now increasingly unable to absorb the impact of rising costs, after its data showed prices increased at the fastest pace in two-and-a-half years this month.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Britain's main retail trade body warned on Tuesday that shops are now increasingly unable to absorb the impact of rising costs, after its data showed prices increased at the fastest pace in two-and-a-half years this month. The British Retail Consortium said shop prices in October were 2.1% higher than a year ago, the biggest increase since February 2024 and up from a 1.4% annual increase in September. "The dam is starting to break on the huge wave of costs retailers have absorbed over the last two years," BRC Chief Executive Helen Dickinson said, calling on finance minister John Healey to lower retailers' property taxes and employment costs in his [USN:L5N46B044 TEXT:"first annual budget"] on Wednesday. Official [USN:L8N46708O TEXT:"consumer price inflation"], which covers a wider range of goods and services, rose to an 11-month high of 3.5% in September from 3.1% in August BRC food price inflation was 2.9% in October, its highest since April and up from 2.5% in September Ambient food price inflation rose to its highest since September 2025 at 3.2%, up from 2.2% in September Fresh food inflation was unchanged at 2.6% Non-food inflation rose to 1.7% from 0.8%, its highest since December 2023, with particularly sharp rises for furniture, flooring and home improvement goods The BRC said prices were being pushed up by higher transport and energy costs, as well as increases in employment costs and packaging levies Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey said this month that businesses had so far [USN:L1N46202H TEXT:"largely absorbed higher energy costs"] caused by the US-Iran war, unlike after Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022, reducing the need to raise interest rates Food price inflation has been slower to pick up than first predicted, with the Food and Drink Federation trade body now expecting it to [USN:L8N4500SL TEXT:"peak next year"] BRC data is based on prices collected from October 1-7
